item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are one loss away from getting swept in the postseason for the first time since the 2023 NLDS against the Diamondbacks. No matter how you want to slice it, they’ve looked inferior in every facet of the game in this series, from situational hitting to defense, bullpen work, and so on—now it’ll be up to Tyler Glasnow to at the very least delay what appears to be an unavoidable postseason exit for the reigning back-to-back champs.
Although the Brewers have yet to formally announce a starter, all signs point towards Dustin May taking the ball in Game 4 of this series—it might be with an opener, or it might be with him as a starter; either way, the bulk innings role will belong to the former Dodger.
When it comes to lineup decisions, Max Muncy figures to regain a starting role at third base, and you have to wonder if Will Smith remains in the seventh spot—the Dodger catcher was responsible for the only big hit the home team had in a Game 3 loss. Speaking of hitters who moved down in the order, although it amounted to very little, Shohei Ohtani reached safely in three of his four plate appearances in a 6-2 defeat.
Neither Evan Phillips nor Roki Sasaki had especially lengthy appearances off the bullpen, so apart from Justin Wrobleski, there’ll be no one else unavailable in the bullpen for Game 4. With nothing to lose and following the seventh-inning debacle of leaving Blake Snell in too long, expect potential aggressive calls to the bullpen at the first sign of trouble for Glasnow.
NLCS Game 4 info
- Teams: No. 2 seed Dodgers vs. No. 1 seed Brewers
- Series: Milwaukee leads, 3-0
- Ballpark: Dodger Stadium, Los Angeles
- Start time: 5:08 p.m.
- TV: FS1 (Joe Davis, John Smoltz, Ken Rosenthal, Tom Verducci)
- National radio: ESPN Radio (Jon Sciambi, Doug Glanville)
- Local English radio: AM 570 (Charley Steiner, Rick Monday)
- Local Spanish radio: KTNQ 1020 AM (José Mota, Luis Cruz)

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dave Roberts' Blake Snell decision was the tip of the iceberg in mortifying Dodgers Game 3 loss
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins

In Game 2, Roberts had Brock Stewart intentionally walk Brice Turang in the sixth to get to the Brewers' hottest hitter in William Contreras, for seemingly no other reason than that the righty-righty matchup looked favorable on paper. Contreras hit a go-ahead single on the
item.content:encoded:
Dave Roberts has not been at his best in the NLCS, with the Los Angeles Dodgers facing the league-best Milwaukee Brewers in a best-of-seven that's making LA's NLDS against the Atlanta Braves look like the smallest of potatoes.
In Game 2, Roberts had Brock Stewart intentionally walk Brice Turang in the sixth to get to the Brewers' hottest hitter in William Contreras, for seemingly no other reason than that the righty-righty matchup looked favorable on paper. Contreras hit a go-ahead single on the first pitch Stewart served him.
That was small potatoes in contrast to Game 3, where Roberts seemed to make the worst possible decision at every conceivable turn. There is, of course, leaving Blake Snell in after he walked Andrew Vaughn to lead off the seventh, which then turned into a go-ahead, two-run homer for Jake Bauers ... and then a solo homer for Garrett Mitchell for some insurance.
The Dodgers went down 6-2, and their backs are now firmly against the wall. Roberts' Snell decision is the one that's going to be remembered least fondly, but there was a parade of other choices that all but doomed LA's three-peat hopes.
Dave Roberts' Blake Snell decision is obscuring smaller mistakes that doomed the Dodgers in NLCS Game 3
Roberts' next greatest sin, perhaps, was burning Josue De Paula in the bottom of the sixth. After Will Smith broke out of his slumber to hit a bases-loaded, go-ahead double, Roberts replaced Miguel Rojas with left Josue De Paula to face righty Abner Uribe. Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy countered by bringing in lefty DL Hall, so Roberts figured he would do play 3D chess and instead offered up righty Kiké Hernández, rendering De Paula unavailable for the rest of the game. Hernández struck out swinging.
There's the fact that Roberts started Tommy Edman, who had a single hit coming into Game 3. He went 0-for-4 on Wednesday night. There's the fact that he put Justin Wrobleski, who had a 6.13 ERA in the second half and was briefly demoted to Triple-A, in the game with the Dodgers down by two. Wrobleski quickly threw a wild pitch that allowed the Brewers' fifth run to score.
It might be going a little too far to say that this showing was legacy-threatening ... but it sure does feel like that right now. Roberts, no doubt, will be appropriately self-critical if the Dodgers' postseason road comes to an end after this series, but that doesn't erase how inexplicable his decisions in Game 3 were, and that they, alone, might've doomed LA.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Max Muncy gives blunt assessment of Dodgers' performance vs. Brewers in NLCS: 'We're playing like s***'
item.dc:creator: Chris Cwik
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are suddenly in big trouble. After yet another loss Wednesday, the Dodgers find themselves down 3-0 in the National League Championship Series. With another loss, they'll be eliminated from the postseason. This wasn't the way it was supposed to be. In year's past, the Dodgers' depth and financial muscle won out against the best teams in the game. Something is different this time around and Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy thinks he knows exactly what's going on. When asked
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are suddenly in big trouble. After yet another loss Wednesday, the Dodgers find themselves down 3-0 in the National League Championship Series. With another loss, they'll be eliminated from the postseason.
This wasn't the way it was supposed to be. In year's past, the Dodgers' depth and financial muscle won out against the best teams in the game. Something is different this time around and Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy thinks he knows exactly what's going on.
When asked, Muncy summed things up succinctly saying, "We're playing like s***."
"It's a pretty simple answer: We're playing like s*** they're playing great."
Max Muncy after the Dodgers dropped Game 3 of the NLCS. pic.twitter.com/0MRmqhpnDk
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 15, 2026
Muncy, of course, made sure to give the Milwaukee Brewers credit. After lamenting his own team's struggles, Muncy added, "[The Brewers] are playing great. It's as simple as that."
Much has been made of the struggles of Dodgers two-way star Shohei Ohtani this postseason, but he wasn't the problem Wednesday. After being dropped to sixth in the batting order, Ohtani reached base three times in the contest.
His overall numbers, however, are still a problem, as Ohtani is hitting just .182 in the series. Many of his teammates have similar batting averages, including Freddie Freeman, Teoscar Hernandez and Muncy, none of whom is hitting above .192. Catcher Will Smith is hitting under .100.
While those struggles can be written off as small-sample outcomes … the NLCS is a small sample. All it takes is a few bad games from your star players to decide the outcome of a series. The Dodgers are experiencing that phenomenon right now.
Because of that, though, it won't take much for the Dodgers to claw their way back into the series. While 3-0 comebacks are highly unlikely, they are not impossible. All it would take is the Dodgers' stars hitting like they should.
Even then, that might not be enough. In order to stage a comeback, the Dodgers also need the Brewers to give them an opening, which seems unlikely given how well Milwaukee is playing right now.

After the g
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers' Miguel Rojas slaps LA with reality check amid 3-0 NLCS deficit vs. Brewers appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are staring at the brink of elimination, and Miguel Rojas is not sugarcoating how they got there. Los Angeles fell 6-2 to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series on Wednesday at Dodger Stadium, putting the two-time defending champions in a 3-0 series hole.
After the game, the veteran infielder offered a blunt explanation for the deficit. "To win championships, you've got to win moments. We haven't been able to do that in this series. They have," Rojas said, via MLB Network. "That's why we're 0-3 right now."
Game 3 was a perfect example. The Dodgers grabbed a 2-1 lead in the sixth inning when Will Smith lined a two-run double off Abner Uribe, and Blake Snell had retired 14 straight batters at one point after allowing a leadoff home run to Jackson Chourio on the first pitch of the game.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Milwaukee flipped it in the seventh. With a runner on, Jake Bauers won an 11-pitch battle against Snell and drilled a two-run homer to put the Brewers back in front. Garrett Mitchell followed with a solo blast, and Milwaukee tacked on runs in the eighth and ninth to pull away.
The big moments have gone the Brewers' way all series. Milwaukee won Game 1 by a 2-1 margin before taking Game 2 7-4, with its bullpen retiring all 15 Dodgers it faced to close out the second game.
The Dodgers' offense, meanwhile, has gone cold. Los Angeles has yet to hit a home run in the series, and it has struggled badly with runners in scoring position throughout the postseason.
Rojas knows the value of a big moment better than most. The 37-year-old is playing his final MLB season after returning to the Dodgers on a one-year deal, and he was one of the heroes of last year's World Series run.
Now, Los Angeles needs a lot of them in a hurry. The Dodgers have trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series only once before, when the Baltimore Orioles swept them in the 1966 World Series.
They will try to stave off elimination in Game 4 on Thursday at Dodger Stadium, with the Brewers looking to complete a sweep and clinch their first National League pennant.
Related: Dodgers' Kyle Tucker makes 1 thing clear with LA facing NLCS elimination

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers' Blake Snell Explains What Went Wrong in Pivotal 7th Inning
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell detailed what went wrong in that all-important seventh inning that turned what had been an excellent outing into disaster against the Milwaukee Brewers in the 2026 National League Championship Series. How did Blake Snell play in the NLCS? Snell started the game by giving up a home run on his first pitch, but after that, he was absolutely dominant, striking out nine batters in the next six innings. That seventh inning, though, was one to forget. The Dodgers
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell detailed what went wrong in that all-important seventh inning that turned what had been an excellent outing into disaster against the Milwaukee Brewers in the 2026 National League Championship Series.
How did Blake Snell play in the NLCS?
Snell started the game by giving up a home run on his first pitch, but after that, he was absolutely dominant, striking out nine batters in the next six innings.
That seventh inning, though, was one to forget.
The Dodgers had just gained their first lead of the night on a two-RBI double by Will Smith in the bottom of the sixth inning, but in the top of the seventh, Snell began by walking Andrew Vaughn.
After that, Snell took on Jake Bauers for an 11-pitch at-bat that ended with a monster two-run home run.
The next batter, Garret Mitchell, also homered, quickly turning the Dodgers’ advantage into a 4-2 Brewers lead.
Snell was then pulled from the game, and Milwaukee would only add to the lead from there, creating a 3-0 series lead that will be nearly impossible for the Dodgers to overcome.
It also created a lot of questions among Dodgers fans, including how Snell’s performance yo-yoed so wildly over the course of his start.
Blake Snell breaks down what went wrong against Brewers
After the game, Snell told reporters that it’s “pretty frustrating” to give up three home runs, especially seeing as he hadn’t even given up one homer in his limited playing time this season.
“It’s something I’ve got to learn from, it’s part of their journey too, and it’s only going to make me better in the long run,” he said from the clubhouse.
Snell also discussed the Bauers at-bat, noting that he’s known Bauers for years and after the Brewer’s up-and-down career, “he’s earned it.”
“Hats off to him. What an at-bat,” he said. “I threw everything I had. Fastball down the middle, if I could locate that better, who knows what would have happened? This is the best I’ve ever seen him play. It’s a good at-bat. Hats off to him.”
Snell also addressed the Dodgers facing elimination and a possible sweep at Dodger Stadium on Thursday.
The game will begin at 5 p.m. PT, not 6 p.m. PT as originally announced.
“Yeah, it sucks, but it’s part of it,” he said. “How do we bounce back, how do we fight? I think that’s the most important thing, us coming together and finding a way to win.”

Two pitches later, he watched another ball fly over the fence, this time off Garrett Mitchell’s bat. The Dodgers’ 6-2 loss
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
Blake Snell stood on the mound with his hand on his hip, waiting for Jake Bauers to cross the plate before punching in his pitch call for the next batter.
The Dodgers left-hander had just given up the lead on Bauers’ two-run homer, spoiling what had been a stellar start Wednesday night at Dodger Stadium. But Snell was ready to move on.
Two pitches later, he watched another ball fly over the fence, this time off Garrett Mitchell’s bat.
The Dodgers’ 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, after the visitors regained the lead with back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning, gave the Brewers a commanding 3-0 lead and set up an elimination game Thursday. After setting their sights on a history-making three-peat, the Dodgers will have to win the next four games just to advance to the World Series.
The Dodgers showed signs of life during Game 3 of the NLCS, but Bill Plaschke writes the reigning champs can’t survive their crushing collapse.
For five innings, the only run on the board was the one the Brewers scored on the first pitch of the game.
Snell zipped a 97.6-mph fastball over the center of the plate, and Brewers leadoff hitter Jackson Chourio sent it into the first row of the stands in right-center.
For much of Snell’s start, however, that aggressive approach worked. He dotted the upper rail with his fastball, threw his curveball for both swings and misses and called strikes, and mixed in his changeup to right-handed batters.
Unlike Snell’s last postseason start, when he issued five walks and lasted just 3-2/3 innings against the Atlanta Braves, his efficiency got him through six-plus innings Wednesday, with just two walks.
And while Snell’s fastball averaged 97 mph in his last start — something he’d done only twice before in his career, regular season or postseason, and not since 2022, according to Statcast — he threw even harder on Wednesday: 97.3 mph.
After Chourio’s home run, Snell retired 18 of the next 20 batters, including 14 in a row, to get through six innings. His nine strikeouts were one shy of a postseason career high, which he recorded against the Brewers last year in Game 1 of the NLCS.
Then in the seventh inning, he issued a leadoff walk to Andrew Vaughn and surrendered back-to-back homers, and suddenly the game had flipped.
With the way the Brewers’ bullpen pitched in the first two games, it seemed the Dodgers would have to score against the Brewers’ starters to have a chance to pull themselves out of the hole they’d dug.
They failed to do so in Game 3, logging just three hits off left-hander Robert Gasser.
Luckily for them, pitching every game of the postseason seemed to finally have caught up to hard-throwing right-handed Abner Uribe in his seventh appearance.
Uribe took over for Gasser in the sixth inning and walked the first two batters he faced.
Then Dodgers manager Dave Roberts had left-handed-hitting Max Muncy pinch-hit for Andy Pages. Muncy struck out, and the biggest moment of the game fell to two Dodgers who have had the worst postseason production on the team.
Roberts had moved Shohei Ohtani down to sixth in the batting order and put Will Smith behind him. Naturally, the game found them.
Ohtani drew a five-pitch walk without taking a swing. With the bases loaded, it was up to Smith, who had gone one for 25 in the postseason to that point.
He ambushed a first-pitch sinker and drove it into the left-field gap for a two-run double and the lead.
The rally halted there. Roberts burned rookie Josue De Paula as a pinch-hitter, swapping him out for Kiké Hernández when the Brewers brought in left-hander DL Hall. Hernández and Tommy Edman struck out to end the inning.
The Dodgers could not keep pace with the Milwaukee Brewers, falling 6-2 Wednesday night in Game 3 of the NLCS and dropping to 3-0 in the series.
Then, three Brewers batters into the seventh, the Dodgers were down 4-2.
Snell hadn’t allowed a home run all year — not in his nine regular-season starts, or in his NLDS appearance. Three on Wednesday defined his start.
The next inning, the Brewers added an insurance run with back-to-back singles against right-handed reliever Roki Sasaki and a wild pitch from left-hander Justin Wrobleski. They tacked on another in the ninth with a pair of singles and a stolen base off Wrobleski.
With the flash of red tail lights flickering outside of the stadium, a sign of Dodgers fans already heading for the exits, Dodgers hitters went down in order in the final half inning.

item.title: [FanSided] 3 mistakes the Dodgers made with their money that cost them a chance at a three-peat
item.dc:creator: Zachary Rotman

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have won back-to-back World Series titles thanks largely to historic spending. A full14 players on the Dodgers' roster are making eight figures this season, and Tarik Skubal (who is making $32 million overall, but $9.5 million prorated after the Dodgers acquired him) isn't far behind from making that 15. For reference, the Mets, the team closest to L.A. payroll-wise, ended the year with just eight players making eight figures this season.
Most of those deals are ones the Dodgers would sign off on again. Even guys who have struggled this postseason, like Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, Shohei Ohtani and Will Smith, have done so much for this team in recent years that it's hard to say the Dodgers should regret paying them. These three deals, though, are ones that the Dodgers should regret offering, now that their three-peat dreams are officially on life support.
OF Kyle Tucker
This is the obvious one. The Dodgers, even after winning back-to-back World Series titles, elected to give Kyle Tucker a four-year, $240 million deal in free agency. When that deal was signed, most MLB fans practically handed the World Series title to L.A., knowing how good Tucker had been in Houston. Instead, Tucker wound up having the worst year of his career.
He slashed .233/.330/.385 with 17 home runs and 70 RBI. He was better down the stretch and has been arguably their best hitter in the postseason, but he's just 2-for-8 in the NLCS. That's not good enough for a player making $60 million a year on average. For reference, Juan Soto's AAV is at $51 million, and he's performed at an MVP level. If the Dodgers got to do it again, they almost certainly wouldn't have made this kind of investment in Tucker.
RHP Edwin Diaz
Tucker wasn't the only high-end free agent the Dodgers signed. They gave Edwin Diaz a three-year, $69 million deal to be their closer, one year after giving Tanner Scott a four-year, $72 million deal to perform in that same role. Scott's first year in L.A. was one to forget, and Diaz followed that same path, posting an 8.68 ERA in 21 games and missing much of the season due to injury.
Diaz was better in the postseason, but given how well Scott performed this season and how lackluster this Dodgers lineup proved to be, wouldn't Andrew Friedman have preferred to give that kind of major money to a big bat? Hindsight is 20/20, but had they known the offense would look this bad in October, they likely would've spent their resources on another bat and let Diaz sign elsewhere.
OF Teoscar Hernandez
Teoscar Hernandez had a huge year in 2024, leading to the Dodgers re-signing him on a three-year, $66 million deal that offseason. That contract made some sense, but handing a power-hitting corner outfielder over the age of 30 a hefty multi-year deal has the risk of backfiring — and this one did almost immediately. Hernandez's 103 OPS+ in 2025 was his worst in a full season in his career, and while he was a bit better overall in 2026, his streakiness and his numbers against righties (.695 OPS) left a lot to be desired.
Those struggles have continued into the playoffs, with Hernandez going 5-for-26 overall and 2-for-10 in the NLCS thus far. Dave Roberts has consistently hit him in the heart of the Dodgers' order, but Hernandez has not been able to come through. There're plenty of other players making the $20+ million that Hernandez is who could've come through for L.A. offensively. With another guaranteed year on his deal, this contract feels like another one that the Dodgers regret.

item.title: [Orange County Register] Brewers push Dodgers to the brink, hit 3 homers off Blake Snell for 3-0 NLCS lead

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Reach out and feel the drywall. The Dodgers’ backs are up against it.
The plucky little team that doesn’t hit home runs hit three of them off of Blake Snell on Wednesday night. The Milwaukee Brewers handed the Dodgers a 6-2 defeat in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, pushing the back-to-back champions to the brink of elimination with the possibility of a sweep to avenge the one the Dodgers handed them last year.
“It’s a pretty simple answer,” Max Muncy said when asked how the Dodgers find themselves in this position. “We’re playing like (profanity). They’re playing great. It’s as simple as that. No need to overcomplicate it.”
Dreams of a three-peat on life support, the Dodgers’ thoughts now have to be on a ‘four-peat’ – it will take four consecutive victories for them to become just the second team in MLB history to come back from a 3-0 deficit to win a best-of-seven series. The 2004 Boston Red Sox (featuring a key stolen base by a reserve outfielder acquired at midseason from the Dodgers) did it in the American League Championship Series against the New York Yankees.
“If we lose, we’re done. We’ve got to go on one-game winning streaks four games in a row,” Kike’ Hernandez said.
“At the beginning of this year, we set out to do something historic,” Muncy said. “It looks like we’re going to have to make a little more history along the way if we want to accomplish that. That’s the task ahead of us. We still have the pitching staff to be able to do it. We just have to get some hits. If we can back our pitching staff then I know that, like I said, we have the pitching staff to do it.”
Tyler Glasnow is scheduled to start Game 4 on Thursday and try to save the Dodgers’ season. Muncy is correct — Glasnow won’t be able to do it without someone applying paddles to the Dodgers’ flatlining offense.
The Dodgers might not be going down without a fight. But so far, they are going down without any of the things it takes to make an offense successful in the postseason.
They are 2 for 16 with runners in scoring position in this series, 3 for 32 in the postseason. They have just two two-out hits in the three NLCS games (both singles) and only two extra-base hits (both doubles). The Dodgers hit 204 home runs in the regular season (tied for fourth in the National League) and eight more in their four-game National League Division Series victory over the Atlanta Braves (the most in the postseason to that point). They have hit none in the NLCS.
“They’re really good pitchers,” Miguel Rojas said. “A lot of their pitchers throw three different fastballs. They throw hard. They’ve been locating the ball really well. They haven’t really given us too many opportunities to build momentum.
“They’ve been attacking the zone. They trust their stuff in the zone. With all three fastballs, with a lot of guys that have a cutter, a sinker and a four-seam fastball, it’s really hard to kind of put barrels on the ball. So you’ve got to build some momentum that you can create with hits, but we haven’t been able to get a big hit.”
The Brewers have grabbed any momentum right back from the Dodgers. The Dodgers have scored in just five of the 27 innings so far. Four of those five times, the Brewers responded by scoring in the next half-inning themselves.
It happened again to turn Game 3.
Snell hadn’t give up a home run this year but Jackson Chourio sent the first pitch he threw Wednesday into the right-field pavilion. Snell thoroughly dominated the Brewers through six innings after that. He retired 18 of 20 batters after Chourio’s home run, striking out nine. Through the first five innings, the Brewers swung at 32 of Snell’s pitches and missed (17) more times than they made contact.
But the Dodgers’ lifeless offense did nothing against the Brewers’ second consecutive rookie starter, Robert Gasser, who held them scoreless on three hits and a walk through five innings.
Brewers manager Pat Murphy went to his bullpen after that, calling on Abner Uribe for the seventh time in their seven postseason games. When Uribe took the mound, the Brewers’ relievers had pitched 9⅔ scoreless innings in the NLCS and had allowed just one earned run in 28⅔ innings this postseason.
But Uribe walked the bases loaded, retiring just one batter. That brought up Will Smith – 1 for his first 25 this postseason. Smith jumped on a first-pitch fastball from Uribe and lined it off the wall in left-center field for a two-run double and a 2-1 lead.
It was the kind of clutch hit that Smith has provided time and time again over the years and had the stadium rocking.
Murphy made his next move, bringing in left-hander DL Hall with runners at second and third. Hall struck out pinch-hitter Kiké Hernandez and Tommy Edman as the Dodgers failed to capitalize on a chance to break the game open.
Snell went back out for the seventh inning having retired 14 in a row. But he walked Andrew Vaughn to start the inning and bring up Jake Bauers whose 12-pitch walk in the third inning of Game 2 was a critical turning point against Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
He did it again, extending his at-bat against Snell for 11 pitches and sending the last one, a fastball over the heart of the plate, into the right-field seats for a two-run home run. Two pitches later, Snell floated a changeup over the middle and Garrett Mitchell sent it on the same flight path as Bauers’ drive.
In 1,200⅔ career innings (regular season), Snell has only given up 15 home runs to left-handed hitters. Bauers and Mitchell did it back-to-back. The Brewers hit 154 home runs during the regular season, the fewest in the National League. They have outhomered the Dodgers 5-0 in the NLCS.
“I mean three home runs in a game — I didn’t give up one the whole year,” Snell said. “To have three in a game is pretty frustrating.”
The Brewers added single runs in the eighth and ninth innings to pull away.

item.title: [NBC Sports] Will Smith drives in only two runs for Dodgers in loss

item.description:
Will Smith hit a two-run double in a Game 3 of the NLCS loss to the Brewers on Wednesday.
Smith gave the Dodgers a 2-1 lead with a bases-loaded double in the sixth inning off Abner Uribe. It’d be the last run of the night for Los Angeles, and the defending champions are now a loss away from their season coming to a close. Smith has been awful in this postseason, and even with the two-run double he’s hitting just .074 over the first seven games.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- The Dodgers' dreams of winning a third straight World Series are quickly fading.
The defending champion Dodgers are in danger of being swept by the Brewers after Milwaukee beat Los Angeles 6-2 to take a 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series.
After a Will Smith double gave the Dodgers a 2-1 lead in the sixth inning, the Brewers immediately answered in the seventh with two home runs off Blake Snell: a two-run blast by Jake Bauers, followed by a solo shot by Garrett Mitchell.
Milwaukee added a run in the eighth after a wild pitch that brought in a runner from third base. The Brewers added another run in the ninth.
Jackson Chourio hit a solo homer on the first pitch of the game.
Los Angeles now faces a must-win game Thursday at Dodger Stadium. Tyler Glasnow is set to pitch for the Dodgers.
This is a developing story. This article will continue to be updated as more information becomes available.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are running out of games to lose if they want to advance to the World Series for a third straight season.
LA is currently down 2-0, but the NLCS has shifted to Los Angeles, which could the Dodgers a slight edge over the next two games (at home).
Moments before the huge Game 3 between the Brewers and Dodgers, a piece of off-field news surrounding Will Smith emerged.
More MLB on Heavy: Max Muncy News Emerges Before Pivotal Brewers-Dodgers NLCS Game 3
Will Smith Becomes Dad to Third Child!!
Just moments before the pivotal Game 3 against the Brewers, Will Smith's wife, Cara, announced a major piece of life news for the Smith family.
She has successfully given birth to her and Will's third child!
Here is the post the two share on Instagram, and they hint that their new daughter's name is 'Carter':
Perhaps this huge piece of life news can get Will Smith going at the plate in the NLCS, as the Dodgers' 2025 World Series hero has slumped since the beginning of the MLB playoffs.
Perhaps being at home will help wake Will Smith regardless.
However, either way, huge congrats to the Smith family for adding a new member to their growing family.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Quietly Announce Roster News on 6-Year MLB Player
Taking a Quick Look at Will Smith's MLB Career
Will Smith is a 3X World Series champion with the Los Angeles Dodgers. He's also been named to the MLB All-Star team three times.
Since making his MLB debut in 2019, Smith has spent his entire 8-year career with the Dodgers.
Over 795 total games played in his career, Smith has 138 home runs, 137 doubles, 476 RBI, and a lifetime OPS+ of 127.
He's been a lifeline for the Dodgers offense in many big moments in his career, and the Dodgers will continue to call his name during the playoffs.

item.title: [New York Post] Blake Snell’s seventh-inning meltdown turns Dodgers’ lead into a nightmare
item.dc:creator: Thomas L Murray

item.content:encoded:
For as good as Blake Snell was in Game 3 of the NLCS on Wednesday night, it was the long ball that got the best of him.
Snell, who came into the postseason without giving up a home run during the regular season, gave up three to the Brewers.
Snell spent most of the night playing from behind, as he put himself in a 1-run deficit after Jackson Chourio blasted a solo shot over the right center field wall, from a 97.6 mph fastball.
Snell went ahead and settled in afterward striking out nine batters and giving up two hits before disaster struck in the seventh.
After his catcher Will Smith got him his first lead of the night in the sixth inning, Snell immediately gave it back up.
When Snell took the mound in the seventh, he opened the inning by giving up a walk to Andrew Vaughn.
Brewers manager Pat Murphy quickly removed him from the game and put in Christian Yelich as a pinch runner.
Murphy’s move wouldn’t end up being a factor as Jake Bauers had other plans.
Bowers and Snell had a long 11-pitch at-bat, where he showed plenty of muscle, including on the 10th pitch when he hooked a ball foul, resulting in it landing just outside of a home run.
On the 11th pitch, he made up for the previous swing by launching a 97.8 mph four-seam fastball over the right field fence for a 412-foot home run.
In the next at-bat, Milwaukee tacked on an insurance run when Snell left a changeup hanging in the center of the strike zone — landing 428 feet over the center field fence to give Los Angeles a 4-2 deficit.
Snell was replaced after the home run and finished the night giving up only four hits, four runs and two walks.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dave Roberts Explain Dodgers' Lineup Shuffle for Game 3

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Shohei Ohtani will hit sixth Wednesday as Dave Roberts reshapes the Dodgers’ lineup for Game 3 against Milwaukee. Kyle Tucker moves to cleanup, Will Smith bats seventh, and Miguel Rojas starts against left-hander Robert Gasser, with Max Muncy available off the bench. Roberts said the changes give the order better balance and make it tougher for Milwaukee to work through its pitching matchups. With the Dodgers down 2–0, he also spoke about Ohtani’s late-night work and the intensity he expects from starter Blake Snell.
“Shohei’s all on board”
Roberts sees Tucker as a good fit in the middle of the order against both Gasser and the relievers who may follow him.
“I love the length of the lineup,” Roberts said. “Kyle has been, throughout his career and currently, agnostic with pitchers left versus right. Gasser is a guy they’re probably going to run two times through the lineup. If it gets a little beyond that, I like Kyle there.”
Smith moves down again after batting fifth in Game 2. Roberts hopes a different spot will help the catcher’s at-bats fall into place.
“Give the player a different look, let the game come to him,” he said. “Last game, there were some good swings in there, which I’m really encouraged about. Having him there around the wraparound of the lineup, I think, is going to be a good thing.”
“I’ve got Miggy in there, which I’m excited about, having Miggy versus a left-hander and then deploying Max whenever the time makes sense.”
Ohtani’s move is part of that effort to spread out the left-handed and right-handed bats.
“It’s more what gives our lineup the best balance,” Roberts said. “Separating the lefties, the righties, making it a little more difficult for them to navigate our lineup. Shohei’s all on board. Whatever it takes to win.”
Ohtani puts in the work
Roberts said Ohtani stayed late Tuesday to work on his swing and talk with teammates about beating Milwaukee.
“As far as him as a person, he couldn’t be more of a team player, more agreeable,” Roberts said. “He was here late last night working on his swing, out with the guys and talking about things, how we’re going to beat these guys.”
“God, it couldn’t be more of a joy. This guy is great for our game. He’s great for all of us.”
Roberts saw a sharper focus in that work.
“He expects a lot from himself, obviously, and he hasn’t performed to his expectations,” he said. “It’s up to all of us to do our jobs. But this was a different look from Shohei yesterday.”
“He was determined, and that’s an understatement.”
Snell’s “slow burn”
Snell gets the ball after a disappointing NLDS start against Atlanta. Roberts has noticed a quieter pitcher waiting for his next chance.
“Much more quiet, staying to himself more,” he said. “He’s been really anxious to get another opportunity. Still being a part of the team and cheering for guys, but this has been a slow burn since that last outing.”
“When you see him take the mound today, you’re going to see another level of intensity. For me, it’s making sure you manage that intensity because it’s already a big game.”
Roberts also likes the thought Snell has put into understanding Milwaukee’s approach.
“He’s a very cerebral, thoughtful person,” Roberts said. “To understand the psyche of your opponent is important because it adds to his edge, his focus, knowing how hungry and feisty and tough that team is.”
“Being aggressive to match their intensity, I like that exercise and what he’s been doing.”
Make the relievers work
Roberts wants more sustained at-bats against a Brewers bullpen that has held the Dodgers scoreless through two games.
“Mookie’s done a good job of still winning pitches, competing in at-bats,” he said. “Other guys, we’ve got to have that same level of fight against those guys versus one-, two-pitch outs.”
“Ashby has been very efficient against us. You’ve got to go through the pain of an at-bat, the grind of it, to ultimately have those guys make a mistake. We could do a better job of that.”
Betts’ work has stood out beyond his batting line.
“He’s playing really high-level baseball,” Roberts said. “If you watch the games, he’s seeing a ton of pitches. He’s getting on base. He’s moving guys over, and that’s what you have to do to win playoff games.”
“There are a couple more big hits in there, maybe a homer. I love the way he’s playing. He’s in a good frame of mind right now, and he’s playing next-level shortstop as well.”
Everything goes into tonight
Roberts plans to manage Game 3 with the urgency its place in the series demands.
“We still have to win four games, but the most important game is tonight,” he said. “We’re going to do everything we can to win this one, and our guys understand how important this one is.”
“It’s good to be home. Those guys fed off their crowd, and I’m excited to see some blue towels and some noise tonight and have our guys feed off it.”
For Roberts, keeping the focus on one game also helps keep the task manageable.
“Guys love to compete. I love to compete,” he said. “We all know what’s at stake. It’s going to be fun. There’s some pressure there, but you’ve got to embrace this.”
“When you start thinking about winning four games, I get nervous. But I think we can manage winning a game tonight.”

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Major League Baseball honored Jackie Robinson on Wednesday with every player, coach and umpire wearing his No. 42 to mark the 79th anniversary of the infielder breaking the sport's color barrier.
Robinson made his debut for the Brooklyn Dodgers on April 15, 1947. He went on to win Rookie of the Year honors and become a six-time All-Star and the 1949 National League MVP. He played in six World Series and won his only championship in 1955 with the Dodgers.
"Every player of color who now enjoys our great sport, they owe it to this man," said Bob Kendrick, president of the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum in Kansas City, Missouri.
Robinson made his pro debut with the Kansas City Monarchs of the Negro Leagues in 1945. He was there five months before Dodgers general manager Branch Rickey interviewed him for possible selection to Brooklyn's International League farm club. Rickey wanted to make sure Robinson could withstand the racial antagonism without reacting angrily.
"What he did was incredibly difficult under some of the most harsh circumstances you could ever imagine," Kendrick said. "He had to go out there and deal not only with the racial hatred but he was carrying 21 million Black folks on his back when he walked across those lines. Had he failed, an entire race of people would have failed. That's an enormous amount of pressure. How he did it with such grace, class and dignity is absolutely incredible. And no, we should never forget Jackie Robinson."
The Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets gathered around the center-field statue of Robinson stealing home at Dodger Stadium. Among the Dodgers were Tyler Glasnow, Teoscar Hernandez, Will Smith, Roki Sasaki, Alex Vesia and Will Klein. Shohei Ohtani, who has attended previously, was not there ahead of pitching against the Mets later.
"A special day, especially for me as a Latino. I wouldn't be here if it wasn't because of him," Mets manager Carlos Mendoza said. "Talk about dealing with pressure at this level, imagine what he dealt with back in the day."
The Dodgers' Dave Roberts, one of just two Black managers currently in the majors, told the teams Robinson would be proud that they reflect his dream and vision of what equality and unity would look like.
"My ask is that we remember how we got here," Roberts said.
In New York, Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. wore his pinstripe pants loose and blousy and rolled at the knees the way many players did in the 1940s, including Robinson.
A video commemorating Robinson and narrated by former Yankees pitcher CC Sabathia was played on the stadium scoreboard before the team's game against the Los Angeles Angels.
"You look at the diversity in our game as far as now, worldwide, and Jackie was the start of opening those doors to not just Black players being able to play but Latin America," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said, "and now we have people from all over the globe playing this, and Jackie was the start of all that."
In Pittsburgh, Pirates manager Don Kelly said, "It doesn't seem like one day is enough to really give back to Jackie and what he meant to baseball and to people."
Two of Robinson's granddaughters joined the teams at Dodger Stadium, not far from Robinson's adopted hometown of Pasadena. He was a four-sport star at Pasadena Junior College before going on to UCLA, where the Georgia native was better known for football than baseball.
Last year, a historical marker honoring the Robinson family was unveiled by the city of Pasadena at their former home.
"We're really carrying the legacy now and it's an incredible honor," said granddaughter Ayo Robinson, whose father, David, is Robinson's youngest son. "It's a weight that feels good because it keeps you grounded in what is so important. I feel like the legacy is just as important today as it has ever been."
Robinson's widow, Rachel, turns 104 in July. She lives in New York and still visits the Jackie Robinson Museum.
"She's the strong matriarch of our family, surrounded by love and intention to continue to allow her to live a life that she wanted," said granddaughter Sonya Pankey Robinson, whose father was Jackie Robinson Jr.
Also on hand in Los Angeles were recipients of scholarships from the Jackie Robinson Foundation.
For the first time in at least two decades, the percentage of Black players on Opening Day rosters increased this season. Major League Baseball says 6.8% of players on Opening Day rosters, injured lists and the restricted list were Black, up from 6.2% at the start of the 2025 season and 6.0% at the start of 2024.
"He's an icon," Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy said of Robinson. "To take this day and make it something special says a lot about the character of the game."br/]

item.title: [Heavy.com] Where is Dalton Rushing? Why Dodgers' Catcher Behind Will Smith Isn't Playing in Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers sure would love to have Dalton Rushing right now. Their starting catcher, Will Smith, is 1-for-23 to begin the postseason. He’s clearly playing through injury, but the Dodgers don’t have any choice but to use him. Rushing isn’t even on the playoff roster, either for the NLDS win over the Atlanta Braves or now in the NLCS against the Milwaukee Brewers. The Dodgers fell behind 0-2 in the series in two games that Smith hit in the heart of the order but didn’t do any damage.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers sure would love to have Dalton Rushing right now.
Their starting catcher, Will Smith, is 1-for-23 to begin the postseason. He’s clearly playing through injury, but the Dodgers don’t have any choice but to use him.
Rushing isn’t even on the playoff roster, either for the NLDS win over the Atlanta Braves or now in the NLCS against the Milwaukee Brewers.
The Dodgers fell behind 0-2 in the series in two games that Smith hit in the heart of the order but didn’t do any damage.
They moved Smith down in the lineup for Game 3 of the NLCS, but that’s about all they can do. They don’t have Rushing to call on.
Where is Dalton Rushing?
Dalton Rushing is currently sidelined due to injury.
The injured list doesn’t work the same in the playoffs, but the Dodgers had placed Rushing on the IL for a portion of September.
When he came back from injury, the Dodgers could only use him as a pinch-hitter or as the designated hitter. He couldn’t catch.
Why Isn’t Dalton Rushing Playing?
Rushing’s injury removes a whole facet of his game.
He partially tore the ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his right elbow in August, and he reaggravated it in September while playing catch.
While it’s unclear exactly the status of Rushing’s elbow right now, the premise is that he can’t throw.
A catcher makes as many throws in a game as the pitchers — most not at the same intensity, but they’re always using their arm — and a few times a game, they do need to throw full throttle.
If Rushing is unable to throw at the moment, it doesn’t just remove him from playing catcher. You can’t really play him elsewhere in the field, either.
Apparently the Dodgers didn’t feel it hampered his swing, because they kept hitting him in September.
It would be hard, though, to have a guy on a postseason roster who genuinely wasn’t healthy enough to play the field. The implication of the Dodgers not having Rushing on the roster is simply that, that he’s not able to do it.
There’s always a chance if they rallied to make the World Series that Rushing could be more healed or pose more of a benefit to have on the roster. But since he’s not on the NLCS roster, he can’t play at least until the next round when new rosters would be submitted.
Who is Dodgers’ Backup Catcher?
The Dodgers’ backup catcher behind Smith in the playoffs is Hunter Feduccia.
He came aboard in a trade from the Tampa Bay Rays over the summer.
Feduccia is a prototypical defense-first catcher. He’s not worth starting over Smith unless Smith’s ailments get so bad that he can’t go out there.
It’s just tough for the Dodgers, who are dealing with both Smith and Shohei Ohtani being far from full strength.

item.content:encoded:
The NLCS resumes at Dodger Stadium on Wednesday, with the Dodgers looking to embark on a comeback down 2-0 in the series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
The top three in the lineup remain the same, as Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and Teoscar Hernández hit in the top three spots. The middle of the lineup received an adjustment that comes as little to no surprise with how Shohei Ohtani and Will Smith have hit in the postseason.
Kyle Tucker moves up to cleanup in the starting lineup, the highest spot in the order he's been placed in this October. After a rough regular season, Tucker has found his stride at the plate at the bottom of the lineup, slashing .300/.391/.500 with a home run and two RBI over six games. Tucker has faced Milwaukee's Game 3 starter Robert Gasser twice in his career, collecting three hits across six at-bats including a home run.
Andy Pages has also impressed at the plate this postseason, turning the page on what was a historically awful title run at the plate last year. The 2026 All-Star has five hits across 20 at-bats, with his highlights being his go-ahead, two-run single in Game 4 of the NLDS and for getting the Dodgers on the board against Jacob Misiorowski in Game 1 of the NLCS. Pages has gone hitless since his Game 1 RBI single, but he moves up to fifth in the lineup against Gasser, also the highest spot he's hit in the postseason this year.
The elephant in the room is Shohei Ohtani getting moved all the way down to sixth in the lineup. Ohtani was adamant about playing in Game 3, and Dave Roberts ultimately granted his wish.
"He's adamant he feels good enough to be in there. He's close to finding something with his swing. I feel great about it," manager Dave Roberts said Tuesday just before the Dodgers workout at Dodger Stadium. "He was very convicted that he is onto something mechanically. He was adamant that he can help us. He's well enough to help us win a baseball game. So that's all I needed to hear."
Try as he might to will his way into the lineup, Ohtani has been a detriment offensively since hitting his final regular season home run on Aug. 18 in Denver, and he's carried that funk over the team's six playoff games slashing just .150/.261/.150 with zero RBI. Ohtani had never hit as low as second in the lineup until Game 3 of the NLDS, and it's the first time Ohtani is hitting sixth in the lineup since Sept. 19, 2020 back when he was with the Angels.
Will Smith has also struggled mightily this October, and he slides all the way down to seventh in the starting lineup. Miguel Rojas gets the start at third base over Max Muncy against the left-hander Gasser, and Tommy Edman gets the start at second base, rounding things out in the lineup. Blake Snell makes his first start since getting the ball for Game 2 of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves.

item.content:encoded:
Game 3 of the National League Championship Series between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium is scheduled to start at 5:00 p.m. PDT on Wednesday.
The Brewers won the first two games of the series on Sunday and Monday.
Milwaukee won the first game 2-1 and the second game 7-4.
Before Wednesday’s game, Mookie Betts dropped an honest quote on Shohei Ohtani, who has struggled significantly this postseason.
Dodgers Star Mookie Betts Makes Honest Shohei Ohtani Statement Amid Brewers Series
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 12: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts in the third inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game two of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 12, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images)
“I couldn’t imagine really having the expectations that he has and falling short in a way that it’s not normal for him,” Betts said to reporters, including USA Today’s Bob Nightengale. “Then having to come back and be present in the postseason knowing how important he is to the boys.”
“He’s trying. It’s just really, really hard. It’s really hard to make these slight adjustments in this short amount of time. Like I said, it took me almost two years. I feel for him. I know he’s grinding, he’s working. So we’ll just see. We’ll see how he comes and prepares.”
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 12: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers walks back to the dugout after striking out in the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game two of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 12, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images)
“But I know he’s giving it his all. We can at least lay our heads on a pillow at night knowing that we’ve given it everything.”
This postseason, Ohtani has gone 3-for-20 with seven strikeouts and three walks. He is dealing with biceps and knee injuries.
Looking at NLCS Game 3 Between Dodgers and Brewers
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 11: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers hits a fly ball against the Milwaukee Brewers during the eighth inning in game one of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 11, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images)
The Dodgers considered benching Ohtani for Game 3, but ultimately placed him in the lineup.
Ohtani is batting sixth, a career low, as the DH today.
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 12: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers returns to the dugout after grounding out in the third inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game two of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 12, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images)
Here is the Dodgers’ lineup:
- Mookie Betts SS
- Freddie Freeman 1B
- Teoscar Hernandez LF
- Kyle Tucker RF
- Andy Pages CF
- Shohei Ohtani DH
- Will Smith C
- Miguel Rojas 3B
- Tommy Edman 2B
Left-hander Blake Snell will start for the Dodgers today. Southpaw Robert Gasser is slated to start for the Brewers.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are set for a pivotal Game Three in their NLCS with the Milwaukee Brewers.
Milwaukee holds a 2-0 lead, and if the Dodgers want to advance to the World Series, they must win four of the next five games, which will certainly be a tall task.
However, the series has now shifted to LA, and the Dodgers have another ace in Blake Snell taking the ball on Wednesday evening.
Before the NLCS Game Three, the Dodgers revealed their lineup to try and muster runs off southpaw Robert Gasser, and Max Muncy is not featured in the group.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Issued Strong Anthony Volpe Take Amid Major Decision
Dodgers’ Max Muncy OUT of Game Three Batting Order
Likely due to the Brewers throwing a southpaw the Dodgers way in Game 3, Max Muncy is not featured in the batting order, but he will likely be used in a pinch-hit scenario if Milwaukee deploys a RHP at some in the game to face Miguel Rojas, who is IN at 3B in Muncy’s place.
@UnderdogMLB help break the news of the full Dodgers lineup for 10/14:
Dodgers 10/14: “M. Betts SS F. Freeman 1B T. Hernández LF K. Tucker RF A. Pages CF S. Ohtani DH W. Smith C M. Rojas 3B T. Edman 2B B. Snell SP”
Other lineup notes include: Both Shohei Ohtani and Will Smith dropping in the order, Kyle Tucker getting the start at cleanup, and Teoscar Hernandez batting third.
Tommy Edman is also getting a start, while the Dodgers are relying on a strong start from Blake Snell.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are facing a must-win in Game Three of the NLCS against the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday evening.
The good news for the Dodgers is that the series is shifting back to Los Angeles. Blake Snell will get the start for LA on Wednesday evening, and he will oppose Robert Gasser.
Before the game started, the Dodgers announced their Game Three lineup, which featured a major Will Smith decision.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Blake Snell News Before Pivotal Brewers Game
Will Smith Dropped in Los Angeles Dodgers Batting Order
When the Dodgers Game Three lineup dropped on Wednesday afternoon, it came with a few surprises.
In two big developments, Will Smith and Shohei Ohtani have dropped in the batting order.
Here is the full group, per @UnderdogMLB:
Dodgers 10/14: “M. Betts SS F. Freeman 1B T. Hernández LF K. Tucker RF A. Pages CF S. Ohtani DH W. Smith C M. Rojas 3B T. Edman 2B B. Snell SP”
The flip to Will Smith being demoted in the lineup is that Kyle Tucker has moved up several spots and will bat cleanup against the Brewers’ LHP Gasser.
Shohei Ohtani bats sixth, and Tommy Edman/Miguel Rojas are getting starts in the infield, while Max Muncy gets the pine.
More MLB on Heavy: Toronto Blue Jays Predicted to Poach Yankees All-Star for $80 Million
Taking a Quick Look at Will Smith’s 2026 Season
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – MAY 08: Will Smith #16 of the Los Angeles Dodgers during a 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves at Dodger Stadium on May 08, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
As did many of the Los Angeles Dodgers (at some point in 2026), Will Smith spent a good chunk of time on the Injured List with a neck issue.
He got a handful of starts down the stretch of the regular season, but he’s been really struggling at the plate in the MLB playoffs, and after moving him down for Game Two, manager Dave Roberts is now demoting him to the 7-spot in the lineup.
Perhaps it’s a wake-up call for Smith, but as the Dodgers search for the right lineup combination, having Smith (who is 1-for-20+) in the 3-hole just isn’t going to get things going.
It will be interesting to see if this decision pays off for Roberts and the rest of the Dodgers.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Issued Strong Anthony Volpe Take Amid Major Decision

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers hope to punch back in the NLCS with a home win in Game 3 over the Milwaukee Brewers.
The Dodgers are down 0-2 in the series, but hope isn’t lost; this Dodgers team thrives when it’s backed into a corner. To turn things around, the offense needs to convert on scoring chances.
Dodgers’ Lineup vs. Brewers
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Freddie Freeman, 1B
3. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
4. Kyle Tucker, RF
5. Andy Pages, CF
6. Shohei Ohtani, DH
7. Will Smith, C
8. Miguel Rojas, 3B
9. Tommy Edman, 2B
The Dodgers announced Tuesday that Shohei Ohtani will play despite his struggles and injuries. He will stay in the 6-hole, his lowest spot yet for the Dodgers.
The Brewers are rolling out lefty Robert Gasser, who possesses some matchup problems. Naturally, right-handers Teoscar Hernandez and Andy Pages are moving up from their usual positions.
Will Smith, who has also struggled in the postseason, is moving down to his lowest spot in a while.
Other than shuffling players around, Roberts is sticking with the same group from Game 2, with the only exception being Miguel Rojas at third base while Max Muncy sits.
Who is pitching for the Dodgers?
Blake Snell takes the mound for the Dodgers in the biggest spot of his career. The team needs him to deliver a great outing to keep their three-peat hopes alive against a game Brewers team.
Snell has posted a 1.90 ERA over 42.2 innings this year. In the postseason, he hasn’t been as sharp in one start. He pitched just 3.2 innings in Game 2 of the NLDS, allowing one run but giving up five walks and three hits.
Against this crop of Brewers hitters, they’re hitting only 11-for-64 with a .172 average, a .274 OBP, and 29 strikeouts.
If Snell does well in this game, his legacy as a Dodger and pitcher will grow exponentially.

item.title: [Yahoo] Comentario: Los Dodgers deberían haber excluido a Shohei Ohtani de la plantilla para la fase final
item.dc:creator: Bill Shaikin
item.description: Los Dodgers nunca se desvían de su plan de juego para la temporada regular: ganar los partidos suficientes para asegurarse una exención en la primera ronda de los playoffs y, de este modo, proporcionar a los jugadores todo el tiempo de descanso que necesitan durante el verano para estar en plena forma cuando llegue el otoño. No necesitan apresurar la vuelta de nadie de la lista de lesionados para hacerse con otro título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. Por desgracia para los Dodgers y s
item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers nunca se desvían de su plan de juego para la temporada regular: ganar los partidos suficientes para asegurarse una exención en la primera ronda de los playoffs y, de este modo, proporcionar a los jugadores todo el tiempo de descanso que necesitan durante el verano para estar en plena forma cuando llegue el otoño. No necesitan apresurar la vuelta de nadie de la lista de lesionados para hacerse con otro título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
Por desgracia para los Dodgers y su cada vez más precaria esperanza de lograr un triplete, no siguieron ese plan de juego con Shohei Ohtani. Los Dodgers le fallaron a Ohtani este verano, y ahora solo les queda cruzar los dedos y esperar lo mejor.
La esperanza, como se suele decir, no es una estrategia.
Los Dodgers deberían excluir a Ohtani de la plantilla para la postemporada.
No lo harán. Ni siquiera lo sacarán de la alineación del miércoles.
En medio de los titulares sobre cómo los Dodgers podrían haber dejado a Ohtani en el banquillo para el tercer partido de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional, el entrenador Dave Roberts explicó que la idea era más bien combinar el día libre del martes con un segundo día consecutivo de descanso.
"Nunca fue una decisión de dejarlo en el banquillo", afirmó Roberts.
Read more: Shohei Ohtani estará en la alineación de los Dodgers para el Juego 3 ante Cerveceros
Roberts estableció un paralelismo entre lo que podría haber ocurrido con Ohtani y lo que sí ocurrió con Freddie Freeman durante la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional de hace dos años, cuando los Dodgers proporcionaron lo que el entrenador denominó un "reinicio": un día libre para el equipo, seguido de un día de descanso para Freeman.
"Y acabó ganando el MVP en la Serie Mundial", señaló Roberts.
Freeman llevaba tres semanas jugando con un tobillo lesionado y, aun así, había sido más productivo aquel octubre de lo que lo ha sido Ohtani este. Ohtani lleva tres meses jugando con una lesión en la rodilla y en el bíceps, y los Dodgers ya han probado con descansos intermitentes.
Lo intentaron en septiembre, dos veces. Hicieron hincapié en su semana de descanso antes del inicio de los playoffs. Hablaron mucho de sus días libres antes del inicio de la NLCS.
Han fallado las cuatro veces. Ya basta.
Roberts afirmó que los Dodgers —no solo Ohtani, sino también el cuerpo técnico y el equipo de preparadores físicos— ven progresos. Es cierto, sin duda. Pero hemos oído palabras igualmente alentadoras tras cada uno de los periodos de descanso de Ohtani.
"Estamos escuchando a Shohei, y vamos a apoyarle a tope y a creer en él", dijo Roberts, "y eso es todo".
Ohtani afirmó el martes que sus síntomas han remitido desde que los Dodgers le incluyeron en la lista de lesionados, por el tiempo mínimo. De eso hace ya un mes.
El martes, afirmó que su enfoque puede alternar entre "centrarse en reducir los síntomas y eliminar el dolor y/o simplemente asegurarme de que me muevo bien en el swing".
Hasta ahora no hay pruebas de que esto pueda funcionar, y sí un conjunto de indicios, cada vez más inquietante, de que quizá no sea así.
Ohtani tiene un promedio de bateo de .150 en los playoffs, con tres hits en 20 turnos al bate. De los 39 jugadores con al menos 20 turnos al bate en esta postemporada antes del partido del martes, solo tres tienen un OPS inferior al de Ohtani, que es de .411.
Uno de ellos, el receptor de los Dodgers Will Smith, tiene un hit en 23 turnos al bate. Pero está golpeando la pelota con fuerza: en la NLCS, una bola salió a 102 mph, otra a 101, y todas las bolas salieron con más fuerza que la que Ohtani golpeó con más fuerza.
Esa velocidad de salida: 86 mph.
No ha bateado ninguna bola hacia la derecha en la serie, ni para conseguir un hit ni para ser eliminado.
A lo largo de su carrera en las Grandes Ligas, ha conectado un jonrón cada 14 turnos al bate.
No ha bateado un jonrón desde el 18 de agosto, un lapso de 107 turnos al bate. Ha impulsado una carrera desde entonces; los Dodgers lo colocaron de cuarto bate en el segundo partido.
Y, desde que bateó ese último jonrón, Ohtani tiene un promedio de bateo de .036 contra bolas rápidas lanzadas a 95 mph o más. La velocidad media de las bolas rápidas en esta postemporada: 96,2 mph, según el análisis detallado del analista Mike Petriello sobre todas las formas en que el swing de Ohtani falla.
¿Bolas con efecto? El relevista de los Brewers, JoJo Romero, le lanzó una baja y alejada en el segundo partido, y Ohtani perdió el control del bate al lanzarse para conectar.
Cuando Ohtani habló con los periodistas antes de que comenzaran los playoffs, dijo que quizá no supiera el alcance total de sus lesiones ni lo que tendría que hacer para recuperarse hasta después de la postemporada.
"No he podido comprender bien la causa principal de todo esto", dijo entonces. "Creo que ese proceso tendrá lugar durante la temporada baja, cuando tenga un poco más de tiempo para poder abordarlo. Pero, por ahora, es algo con lo que simplemente tendré que lidiar".
Los Dodgers no necesitaban a Ohtani para ganar la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. Necesitaban dejarlo de lado durante un periodo prolongado para maximizar sus posibilidades de ganar en octubre.
No lo consiguieron. Creían que unos pocos días de descanso les permitirían cuidar a Ohtani durante el resto de la temporada.
Un gran golpe en octubre, ¿y qué más da? Pregúntaselo a Kirk Gibson, quien cojeó hasta el bate y luego conectó uno de los jonrones más dramáticos de la historia de la Serie Mundial.
Esto es lo que los Dodgers deberían tener en cuenta: ese fue el único turno al bate que Gibson tuvo en aquella Serie Mundial de 1988.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Down 2-0 to Brewers, Dodgers try to bring right mindset back to LA
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The Milwaukee Brewers have control of the National League Championship Series, enough so that the two-time defending World Series champions are pondering what was previously believed to be unthinkable. With a relentless offense and a dominating bullpen, the Brewers have a 2-0 lead in the NLCS over the Los Angeles Dodgers with the best-of-seven matchup set to resume on the West Coast on Wednesday. The Dodgers are so troubled about a stagnant offense that they have considered reducin
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Milwaukee Brewers have control of the National League Championship Series, enough so that the two-time defending World Series champions are pondering what was previously believed to be unthinkable.
With a relentless offense and a dominating bullpen, the Brewers have a 2-0 lead in the NLCS over the Los Angeles Dodgers with the best-of-seven matchup set to resume on the West Coast on Wednesday.
The Dodgers are so troubled about a stagnant offense that they have considered reducing four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani to a bench role for at least one game, if not more.
Ohtani is 1-for-7 with a walk in the series and 3-for-20 with three walks in six games this postseason as he looks physically compromised after dealing with left knee and right biceps discomfort for three months.
Los Angeles’ 2025 postseason hero Will Smith is 0-for-7 with a walk in the series and 1-for-23 in the postseason as the Dodgers have averaged 3.2 runs during their six playoff games.
“Grind. Win one game at a time, one pitch at a time,” said Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts, who took over Ohtani’s leadoff spot late in the regular season. “The mindset can’t really change. We can’t add more pressure. There’s already enough as it is. Keep it simple. One pitch at a time. Figure out a way to get a hit.”
They didn’t do much hitting against Milwaukee starters Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson to start the series and did even less against a Brewers bullpen that retired all 15 batters it faced in Game 2.
Milwaukee is now set to send left-hander Robert Gasser (0-0, 2.25 ERA) to the mound in Game 3. The rookie was 5-5 with a 3.87 ERA in 21 regular-season appearances (20 starts) and has already faced the Dodgers twice this season, going 0-2 with a 5.91 ERA.
In the deciding Game 4 of the NL Division Series against the San Diego Padres, Gasser came through with four solid innings, allowing one run in an eventual 3-1 victory.
As for what kind of Dodgers lineup Gasser will face, the Brewers are trying to avoid all the speculation.
“That’s kind of our whole theme coming into this thing: ‘Hey, guys, yeah, they might be this, they might be (that),'” Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. “… That’s for other people to consider. Let’s just play the game the way we play the game, and let’s go right at people and see what we can do. That’s not going to change.”
If there is an area of concern for Milwaukee, it is with a defense that has not been at its best. Henderson had two throwing errors in Game 2.
“It’s what we do in response that matters,” Murphy said. “… They’ve played good defense. There’s going to be miscues. That’s just part of it. It’s what you do on the next play.”
Also looking to improve is Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell (0-0, 2.45), who will be on the mound for Game 3.
Injuries limited Snell to nine regular-season starts, but he went 4-1 with a 1.90 ERA in them. He then walked five and lasted just 3 2/3 innings in Game 2 of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves.
Snell has just three career regular-season starts against the Brewers and none since 2024, going 1-2 with a 5.79 ERA. He did pitch eight shutout innings against the Brewers in last season’s NLCS with 10 strikeouts.
–Doug Padilla, Field Level Media

item.title: [MLB.com] Here's the root of Ohtani's slump. Is there time to fix it?
item.dc:creator: Mike Petriello
item.description: Are the Dodgers really going to bench Shohei Ohtani, of all people, when the NLCS returns to Los Angeles for Game 3 on Wednesday?
