item.content:encoded:
Después de que Sale consiguiera cada uno de sus primeros seis outs por la vía del ponche en el Juego 3 de la SDLN contra los Dodgers, Dubón registró el primer out defensivo y lo hizo de manera espectacular.
Con un corredor en primera y nadie fuera en la parte alta del tercer inning, la exsuperestrella de los Bravos Freddie Freeman conectó un batazo profundo hacia el jardín izquierdo que salió de su bate a 101.3 mph. Dubón siguió la trayectoria de la pelota hasta la pared y calculó perfectamente su salto para realizar la atrapada justo frente a un grupo de relevistas de los Dodgers, quienes se preparaban para que la bola cayera en el bullpen de los visitantes.
La atrapada de Dubón probablemente le robó un posible jonrón de dos carreras a Freeman, pero como mínimo evitó un extrabase y, casi con toda seguridad, una carrera o dos en el episodio.
Los Dodgers llenaron las bases gracias a un sencillo de Will Smith con dos outs y a que Shohei Ohtani llegó a salvo por interferencia del receptor, pero Sale salió ileso al hacer que Miguel Rojas conectara una línea al jardín derecho para terminar la entrada.
Antes de siquiera necesitar la ayuda de su defensa, Sale se unió a Mike Hampton (Juego 2 de la SDLN del 2003) como los únicos lanzadores de los Bravos en conseguir cada uno de sus primeros seis outs por la vía del ponche en un juego de postemporada.
Freeman se desquitó en su siguiente turno al bate, cuando disparó con autoridad un cuadrangular hacia el jardín derecho-central, el 18vo vuelacercas de su carrera en postemporada, para darle a los Dodgers una ventaja de 3-0.

item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
ATLANTA — The Dodgers went into Game 3 of the National League Division Series knowing they couldn’t be so reliant on the home run, especially with Braves ace Chris Sale on the mound. And yet, in a 3-1 win, it was the home run ball, paired with a masterful performance on the mound from right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto, that secured the victory.
The Dodgers pulled ahead to a 2-1 lead in the best-of-five series.
The Dodgers tried to score in other ways, putting on six baserunners in the first three innings of the game. But it didn’t work.
They failed to take advantage of some luck and poor defense from the Braves in the first inning, as Mookie Betts beat out a soft ground ball up the first base line and Teoscar Hernández reached on a fielding error by Braves shortstop Ha-Seong Kim.
Yoshinobu gives up four hits and strikes out 10 and Kiké Hernández hits a two-run home run to power the Dodgers to victory in Game 3 of the NLDS.
The lineup shuffling manager Dave Roberts did against Sale had superstar Shohei Ohtani, batting fifth, walking up to the plate with two outs and runners on first and second. His over-anxious approach at the plate so far this postseason followed him into the at-bat. And he struck out whiffing on a slider in the opposite batter’s box.
The next inning, Kyle Tucker hit a two-out single into left, baited Sale into picking over to first base twice, and then stole second. But he was stranded there, as Kiké Hernández went down swinging. All six of the Dodgers’ outs in the first two innings came via the strikeout.
In the third, the Dodgers loaded the bases. Mookie Betts started the effort with a double through the left side of the infield. And it looked for a moment as if Freddie Freeman had capitalized on the opportunity with a runner in scoring position.
He stayed back on a fastball and crushed it to deep left field, on a trajectory to just clear the short fence. But Braves left fielder Mauricio Dubón made a leaping catch, holding into the ball as he slammed into the wall.
Undeterred, the Dodgers kept putting runners on base. With two outs, Will Smith stayed through a slider to single. Ohtani clipped Braves catcher Drake Baldwin’s mitt and was awarded first base for catcher’s interference. Then Miguel Rojas, who’d exit the game in the eighth inning mid-at-bat with what the Dodgers called low back pain, hit a line drive that found leather to end the inning.
So, back to the long ball.
Perennial postseason hero Kiké Hernández delivered the first blow. With Andy Pages on first, after his first hit of the series, Hernández launched a changeup into the left-field stands. Then, two batters later, Freeman turned on an inside sinker and sent it over the right-field fence — where Dubón had no chance to track it down.
Game 3 was billed as a matchup between aces: Sale, whom the Braves tabbed for Tuesday because of his workload in their wild-card series, and Yamamoto, whom the Dodgers partially held back for the first two games with the NLCS in mind.
Yamamoto held up his end of the bargain, limiting the Braves to four hits and one run in seven innings.
He retired 10 of the first 11 batters he faced. The only baserunner in that time, Michael Harris II, bunted for a single. Yamamoto crashed hard, slipping on the slick grass as he tried to pivot but still managing to make a throw to first from the ground.
Shohei Ohtani is batting fifth in the lineup against Braves ace Chris Sale in Game 3 of the NLDS. He hasn’t hit fifth or lower in a starting lineup since 2020 with the Angels.
He only wavered in the fifth, loading the bases with a pair of singles and a four-pitch walk. The Braves’ batting order turned over, and Yamamoto got Baldwin to ground out to first, but that allowed a run. Then he induced Ronald Acuña Jr. to ground out to second to escape the jam. Rojas ranged to his left to field the ball and made an on-target throw even as he slipped on the grass in shallow right field.
Yamamoto didn’t allow another baserunner.
Left-handed reliever Tanner Scott served as the Dodgers’ setup man, throwing a hitless eighth. And right-hander Edwin Díaz came in for his first save opportunity since Aug. 14 against the Brewers.
He gave up a double off the wall to Ozzie Albies to open the inning but retired the next three batters.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers World Series hero Miguel Rojas exits after experiencing discomfort
item.dc:creator: Thomas L Murray
item.description: During the eighth inning of Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday, Dodgers middle infielder Miguel Rojas exited the game. Rojas was seen in visible discomfort after fouling off a fastball from Braves reliever Brent Suter. Rojas started limping back toward the batter’s box and was immediately evaluated by a member of the Dodgers’ training staff and manager Dave Roberts. Shortly after the injury, the Dodgers announced that Rojas was removed from the game due to lower back pain. Tommy Edman replaced Rojas
item.content:encoded:
During the eighth inning of Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday, Dodgers middle infielder Miguel Rojas exited the game.
Rojas was seen in visible discomfort after fouling off a fastball from Braves reliever Brent Suter.
Rojas started limping back toward the batter’s box and was immediately evaluated by a member of the Dodgers’ training staff and manager Dave Roberts.
Shortly after the injury, the Dodgers announced that Rojas was removed from the game due to lower back pain.
Tommy Edman replaced Rojas at second base.
Rojas went 0-for-3 before departing Tuesday. He has one hit in the series — a double in Saturday’s 5-3 victory.
Rojas is expected to retire after the season is over.
Rojas was a World Series hero last year after hitting a game-tying home run in Game 7 against the Blue Jays, sending the game to extra innings.
The Dodgers went on to win the game in the 11th when Will Smith hit a go-ahead home run.
In Tuesday’s game, the Dodgers’ offense popped off in the fourth inning, when Kiké Hernández and Freddie Freeman homered to give LA a 3-0 lead.
The Braves scored in the fifth when Drake Baldwin grounded out to first after Dodgers starting pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto loaded the bases.
Yamamoto finished with a career-high 10 strikeouts. He tossed 98 pitches in seven innings, giving up four hits, one run and one walk.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are tied with the Atlanta Braves at one game apiece in their best-of-five series in the NLDS.
On Tuesday night, the two teams will meet for Game 3 at Truist Park in Atlanta, with the Braves sending out left-handed ace Chris Sale while L.A. will start right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto in what should be one of the best pitching matchups we’ve seen so far this postseason.
Ahead of the game, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made some major lineup changes, including one involving veteran slugger Freddie Freeman.
Dodgers Announce Freeman Move
With Shohei Ohtani struggling at the plate recently, Roberts decided to move him down to the No. 5 spot in the lineup Tuesday night.
As a result, Freeman will move up from the cleanup spot to the No. 2 spot, while Mookie Betts remains in the leadoff spot.
Teoscar Hernandez and Will Smith will fill the No. 3 and No. 4 spots, while the back end of the order will remain fairly close to what the Dodgers have used recently, despite bringing Andy Pages back into the lineup.
Here’s the full Dodgers lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Dodgers 10/6 M. Betts SS F. Freeman 1B T. Hernández LF W. Smith C S. Ohtani DH M. Rojas 2B A. Pages CF K. Tucker RF E. Hernández 3B Y. Yamamoto SP.”

K. Tucker RF

Y. Yamamoto SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) October 6, 2026
Freeman’s 2026 Postseason
While it’s only been two games, Freeman has been one of the most consistent bats in the Dodgers’ lineup against his former team.
He’s recorded three hits across seven at-bats, including two on Sunday, one of which was a home run.
Freeman spent the first 12 years of his MLB career with the Braves and became one of the greatest players in franchise history. Now, he’ll play the next two games in a ballpark he called home for more than a decade.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Shohei Ohtani dropped to fifth in Dodgers' batting order for Game 3 of NLDS vs. Braves
item.dc:creator: Chris Cwik
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are pushing two-way star Shohei Ohtani to fifth in the batting order following a tepid start to the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves. After hitting second in the first two games of the series, Ohtani was dropped to fifth ahead of Game 3 on Tuesday. Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, Teoscar Hernández and Will Smith will hit ahead of Ohtani in Game 3. In the two previous games in the series, Betts led off and Ohtani hit second. Per The Athletic's Fabi
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are pushing two-way star Shohei Ohtani to fifth in the batting order following a tepid start to the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves.
After hitting second in the first two games of the series, Ohtani was dropped to fifth ahead of Game 3 on Tuesday. Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, Teoscar Hernández and Will Smith will hit ahead of Ohtani in Game 3.
In the two previous games in the series, Betts led off and Ohtani hit second.
Per The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya, Dodgers managers Dave Roberts told reporters that the move to fifth would be just for Tuesday's game against Braves ace Chris Sale. A lefty, Sale has been notoriously tough against left-handed batters over his career.
Roberts added that when he approached Ohtani about moving down in the order on Monday, Ohtani responded that he'd considered suggesting doing so in September as he struggled through injuries.
Hitting fifth is unusual for Ohtani, who hasn't hit that low since 2020, when he was a member of the Los Angeles Angels.
Ohtani hasn't been terrible in the first two games of the series, going 2-for-8 with two strikeouts. But other members of the team have outperformed the slugger in the NLDS. Freeman and Hernández, in particular, have ignited the Dodgers' offense. Smith, however, is hitless in eight at-bats thus far.
At the plate, Ohtani has been worse against lefties over his career, though he still has an excellent .853 OPS against them. That's actually higher than Smith's career OPS against left-handers.
Ohtani, however, came into the playoffs battling multiple injuries. On Friday, he acknowledged that left knee and right biceps issues will impact him throughout the postseason. Those same issues seemed to affect Ohtani in the second half, as he hit .241/.322/.472 in August before collapsing with a .200/.300/.233 line in eight games in September. At that point, the team put Ohtani on the injured list to give him time to recover for the playoffs.
Now that the playoffs are here, the Dodgers will try to ease Ohtani into a bigger role. While he hit second in the order early in the NLDS, a combination of his performance and Sale's presence on the mound will drop Ohtani much lower than he has hit in recent seasons.

Tucker stayed in the dugout, standing up next to dugout fence before heading into the clubhouse after the inning was over. "I really felt it when I went out for defense
item.content:encoded:
MINNEAPOLIS -- Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Kyle Tucker was removed from Monday's game against the Minnesota Twins in the second inning because of low back spasms.
Tucker walked with one out in the second and ran lightly to second base on Tommy Edman's single to right field. Then, Tucker was replaced by pinch runner Alex Call. Tucker stayed in the dugout, standing up next to dugout fence before heading into the clubhouse after the inning was over.
"I really felt it when I went out for defense in between innings in the first," Tucker said. "Went out there and just tried to hope that it could kind of calm down, or go away or something and I could just keep playing through it. ... On the bases and stuff, it was kind of still sticking around, still kind of there."
Manager Dave Roberts said he considered Tucker day-to-day. The outfielder said, "just got to kind of see how it goes tomorrow," regarding his status.
After signing a four-year, $240 million contract with Los Angeles in January, Tucker has played in 75 of the Dodgers' 79 games this season. But he has hit just .234 with six home runs and 40 RBIs. The .234 average is his lowest since hitting .141 in 28 games as a rookie in Houston in 2018. He has hit at least 22 homers in each of the past five seasons.
The Dodgers also pulled catcher Dalton Rushing in the bottom of the third to rule out a concussion. Roberts said Rushing passed concussion testing, but the catcher has to retake the test 24 hours later and probably will be out of Tuesday's lineup. He was replaced by Chuckie Robinson and Roberts said the team probably would add another player in case Rushing is unavailable.
Los Angeles was already without No. 1 catcher Will Smith, who is on the 10-day IL because of neck inflammation.

item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 26: Will Smith #16 of the Los Angeles Dodgers celebrates with Andy Pages #44 after scoring in the top of the fourth inning against the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park on September 26, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images)
If the Los Angeles Dodgers want to advance in the MLB playoffs, their hitters are going to have to get going.
Currently, the NLDS between the Braves and Dodgers is knotted 1-1, but the series is shifting to Atlanta, which may give the Braves a slight advantage.
Before the pivotal Game Three between the Dodgers and Braves, LA’s manager, Dave Roberts, announced a piece of Andy Pages lineup news.
Andy Pages Will be in Dodgers Lineup Against Chris Sale
If you are not aware, the Atlanta Braves are throwing ace starter Chris Sale in Game Three, which means a tall task is ahead for Dodgers hitters.
Andy Pages, who has notably been struggling in the MLB playoffs over the last two years, will be in the lineup against Sale on Tuesday, per Dave Roberts.
@DodgersNation wrote: “Andy Pages will be in the Dodgers NLDS Game 3 lineup today despite his 0-for-7 start to the postseason, per Dave Roberts.”
Roberts also noted (about Pages):
“I’m going to continue to give Andy a leash. I believe in him.”
Andy Pages had a stellar regular season for the Dodgers, but a wrist injury left him sidelined for most of September, and now he’s started to struggle at the plate.
“Andy Pages in his postseason career: Began 1-for-10 (.282 OPS). *2024 NLCS Game 5: 3 hits, 2 HR. Since then: 4-for-63 (.185 OPS). Among 590 players with 80+ PA in the postseason, his .343 OPS ranks 589th”
GettyLOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – AUGUST 15: Andy Pages #44 of the Los Angeles Dodgers warms up before the starts of an inning against the Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
Andy Pages played in 134 games for the Dodgers in the regular season. He posted a bWAR of 6.0, which is a very strong mark.
He batted .274 with 26 doubles, 23 home runs, and an OPS+ of 122 while playing a very strong defensive center field.
Pages was named to the All-Star team for the first in his career back in July, but all the regular-season awards/accolades go out the window during the MLB playoffs.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dave Roberts Ponders Dodger Lineup Tweaks Ahead of Game 3
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: ATLANTA, GA — Dave Roberts spent Monday weighing changes on both sides of the ball before Game 3 in Atlanta. The Dodgers manager said he is considering lineup tweaks against Chris Sale, including the possibility of moving Shohei Ohtani lower in the order. He also made it clear that Edwin Díaz has worked his way back into serious ninth-inning consideration after his sharp outing in Game 2. With the NLDS tied 1-1, Roberts sounded open to adjusting quickly. Díaz Could Close “I think that we’ve buil
item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA, GA — Dave Roberts spent Monday weighing changes on both sides of the ball before Game 3 in Atlanta.
The Dodgers manager said he is considering lineup tweaks against Chris Sale, including the possibility of moving Shohei Ohtani lower in the order. He also made it clear that Edwin Díaz has worked his way back into serious ninth-inning consideration after his sharp outing in Game 2.
With the NLDS tied 1-1, Roberts sounded open to adjusting quickly.
Díaz Could Close
“I think that we’ve built him up, regained the confidence in him and himself,” Roberts said of Díaz. “I think that it’s certainly a viable option for tomorrow night. I feel very confident with him finishing a game.”
Roberts said Díaz’s most recent outing was about as good as he has seen from him.
“That last outing was as good as we’ve seen him throw, and it’s hard to imagine throwing any better,” Roberts said. “He’s put himself in a position to be the closer.
“In October, I don’t pay too much attention to the long sample of a season in a lot of cases, because in October things happen quickly and you’ve got to be willing to read and react.”
Roberts also praised the way Díaz handled a difficult season.
“Character,” he said. “That’s the main thing. When things aren’t going the best and how players respond, that’s telling.
“The way he stayed the course, dealt with the injuries, went to OKC on a longer rehab to work things out and then took on whatever role we had for him says a lot about him.”
Lineup Changes Are on the Table
Roberts also acknowledged that the Dodgers could look different against Sale.
“I am considering it,” he said. “I think that’s a very fair question. I have to be mindful of it being two games, and then within those two games, what have I seen? Are we seeing good at-bats?”
He pointed to Will Smith as someone whose results have not matched the quality of his plate appearances.
“I think Will Smith is taking good at-bats, just missing some pitches, taking good swings, not chasing much,” Roberts said. “Versus other people maybe expanding, trying to do too much.
“Those are things that you’re trying to make bets on. Then you’re looking at tomorrow with Sale, the history, recency, how guys are prepared and will prepare for Sale. So yeah, I’m thinking through that, and there are possible changes.”
Roberts listed Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas and Max Muncy among the options he could work into the lineup.
“At the end of the day, our guys are our guys,” he said. “I can tweak a lineup. I can insert, take out a player or two, but we still have to go out there and play, execute and take good at-bats.”
Moving Ohtani Is Possible
Roberts said he would consider moving Ohtani further down in the order if he believes it helps the team.
“I would,” he said. “I think moving him from one to two, but going further than that, I’m open to it.
“If I do, I would obviously have the conversation with Shohei to explain why. At the end of the day, every conversation I’ve had with him is whatever is best for the team, he’s all in on. I know that undoubtedly.”
Roberts thinks some of Ohtani’s recent issues have come from trying to do too much.
“I think there’s a little bit of trying to do too much,” he said. “Everything orbits around Shohei in the sense of his talent, and the Braves are going to enter with caution. They’re going to continue to expand as long as we keep giving that to them.
“Until we show some discipline, they’re going to continue to use that playbook.”
He also said Ohtani may be pressing for power.
“Hitting homers, slugging is so much a part of his hallmark in the batter’s box,” Roberts said. “He’s very in tune with what’s being said, what he hasn’t done.
“But that base hit the other way yesterday, that’s production. Against a guy like Chris Sale, that gives you a chance. Trying to chase slug tomorrow night might not be the right plan given the starter.”
Roberts Still Believes in Pages
Andy Pages has also struggled, but Roberts said he plans to keep giving him chances.
“I’m going to continue to give Andy leash,” Roberts said. “I believe in him. I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we’re going to need him to be an active part of our team.
“This is, for me, given how he has come into the postseason, too small of a sample. He has taken two walks. Tomorrow is not going to be the end-all, be-all because Sale is a tough matchup, but I still want to see good at-bats.”
Roberts believes the main issue is pressing.
“I think there’s trying to do too much,” he said. “When he came back, he was swinging the bat really well, had success, and now I think there’s a little bit of trying too much.”
Freeman Looks Healthier
One hitter Roberts feels especially good about is Freddie Freeman.
“I think he’s gotten into his legs a lot more,” Roberts said. “He’s moving balls in the hitting zone forward. He’s as healthy as he’s been in quite some time. I think the mechanics are sound.”
Roberts credited the five-day break with helping Freeman get his knee into better shape.
“The week off was really crucial for him,” he said. “Being able to manage that with the five days off got him back to health to be able to work through some things without having to perform in a game setting.”
Sale vs. Yamamoto
Roberts expects Sale to attack the Dodgers much the same way he did when Atlanta faced them in August.
“The fastball just sort of bullied us at the top of the zone,” Roberts said. “There was some chase down below, and with the lefties, throwing more two-seamers to keep us honest in and then expand away.”
Still, Roberts believes the Dodgers are in a better offensive place than they were then.
“I do think we are in a different spot,” he said. “The stakes are certainly higher. There is familiarity on both sides. I think we’ll see better at-bats.
“Chris is going to be tough regardless. We know that. We know we’re going to be in for a dogfight, but I just don’t see him bullying us like he did his last start.”
And Roberts feels good about the pitcher the Dodgers will send out against him.
“There should be a lot of talk about Chris Sale, but our guy’s pretty dang good,” Roberts said. “He’s been a very good pitcher in the postseason, so we feel very good about that.
“I think both pitchers are going to pitch well. It’s kind of who grinds out at-bats best.”

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers World Series hero Miguel Rojas earns US citizenship: ‘I’m really proud of being an American’
item.dc:creator: Thomas L Murray
item.description: As Miguel Rojas is entering the final chapter of a 13-year career, he has a lot to be proud of. One thing that he is certainly proud of happened over the Dodgers’ bye week last week, when he revealed he flew out to Miami to take his citizenship test and passed. “As soon as I made the decision that I wanted to do this, I wanted to do it for my family, for my kids and for the future of them,” Rojas said. “So I’m really proud of being an American.” Rojas, 37, first came to America after he arrived
item.content:encoded:
As Miguel Rojas is entering the final chapter of a 13-year career, he has a lot to be proud of.
One thing that he is certainly proud of happened over the Dodgers’ bye week last week, when he revealed he flew out to Miami to take his citizenship test and passed.
“As soon as I made the decision that I wanted to do this, I wanted to do it for my family, for my kids and for the future of them,” Rojas said. “So I’m really proud of being an American.”
Rojas, 37, first came to America after he arrived as a 16-year-old prospect out of Venezuela with the Cincinnati Reds.
Since then, he’s developed a whole life in the United States, and he and his wife, Marianna Rojas Gamboa have two children that were born here when he was playing with the Miami Marlins.
“I’m proud of being working here for over 20 years now,” Rojas said. “I’ve been playing professional baseball now for a long time, and that gave me the opportunity to learn the culture, the country, and I don’t take that for granted.”
On the baseball field, Rojas has had a lot to celebrate as he is a two-time World Series champion with the Dodgers.
For Rojas, Dodgers fans will always remember him as a World Series hero last year, when he had a game-tying home run in the ninth inning against Toronto Blue Jays closer Jeff Hoffman to even the score at four apiece.
The Dodgers would get the win after Will Smith made World Series history by hitting the first Game 7 extra-innings go-ahead home run.
While the Dodgers are preparing to play Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday against the Atlanta Braves, Rojas’ time on the baseball field will soon be coming to an end, as he announced at the beginning of the season that he plans to retire after the season.
In his 13-year career in the MLB, Rojas has played five seasons with the Dodgers and has a career 19.6 WAR, a .260 batting average, 61 home runs and 386 RBIs.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have faced two bullpen games to kick off their National League Division Series battle with the Atlanta Braves.
On Tuesday, things will get much more difficult.
The Dodgers are going up against 10-time All-Star and former Cy Young award winner Chris Sale. The left-hander is coming off a regular season in which he had a 2.16 ERA and 200 strikeouts over 162.2 innings. He then allowed three runs over 6.1 innings in his wild-card Game 1 start, and pitched 1.1 scoreless innings to close out Game 3.
The Dodgers know what they're up against with Sale, one of baseball's best pitchers.
"Chris is going to be tough," Roberts said. "We know we're going to be in for a dogfight."
The difficult lefty matchup also has manager Dave Roberts considering some lineup changes.
“I think so," Roberts said. "I am considering it. I think that’s a very fair question. I think that I have to be mindful of — it’s two games, and then with the two games, what have I seen?”
Roberts mentioned Enrique Hernandez and Miguel Rojas as potential options to be in the lineup. The only Dodgers with any semblance of success against Sale in their careers are Mookie Betts (7-for-18) and Freddie Freeman (5-for-16).
The Dodgers have been especially reliant on the home run this series, with all seven of their runs coming via the long ball.
In Sunday's Game 2, they went 0-for-8 with runners in scoring position.
Sale faced the Dodgers on Aug. 27, firing a complete-game shutout with 11 strikeouts and just five hits allowed.
Dave Roberts Considering Moving Shohei Ohtani Down in the Lineup
The Dodgers have plenty of players struggling in the lineup, including Will Smith (0-for-8), Andy Pages (0-for-7) and Tommy Edman (0-for-5).
At the top of the lineup, however, is Shohei Ohtani, who is 2-for-8 with two singles and two strikeouts. He's looked far from his usual self.
"I think there's, like we've talked about, he's not 100%," Roberts said on Monday. "But at the end of the day, he can still do a better job of staying in the strike zone. ... I think that's something that — it's hard to have success when you're out of the zone. ... And Shohei understands, any hitter understands that. So I think that's the thing is — then the question is how do we get him into it? I think there's a little bit of trying to do too much. I think that's a piece."
Roberts said he's open to moving Ohtani down in the lineup, especially with the tough left-hander on the mound.
However, he wouldn't commit to anything on Monday.
"Going further than [No. 2]? I'm open to it," Roberts said. "It's something that, if I do, I would obviously have the conversation with Shohei to explain why. And at the end of the day, every conversation I've had with him is, whatever is best for the team, he's all in on.”
For what it's worth, Ohtani is 3-for-15 against Sale in his career with five strikeouts.
"At the end of the day, our guys are our guys," Roberts said. "And, yeah, I can tweak a lineup. I can kind of insert, take out a player or two. But at the end of the day we still have got to go out there and play and execute and take good at-bats."

ATLANTA — As the Dodgers mull potential lineup changes for Game 3 of the National League Division Series, manager Dave Roberts said he is “open” to moving Shohei Ohtani lower in the batting order.
In his three seasons with the Dodgers, Ohtani has batted first or second in every game he has started. However, as he has admitted he is trying to “manage” in the aftermath of knee and arm injuries, and as Roberts has acknowledged Ohtani is “not 100%,” the lack of success could compel the manager to replace him at the top of the lineup with a more productive hitter at some point.
“I would,” Roberts said Monday. “I would. I think it’s something that, you know, I think moving him from 1 to 2 — but going further than that? I’m open to it.
“And it’s something that if I do, I would obviously have the conversation with Shohei to explain why. And at the end of the day every conversation I’ve had with him is whatever’s best for the team, he’s all-in on. So I know that undoubtedly.”
It would be strange for the Dodgers to bench Shohei Ohtani, but it’s clear that pretending he’s healthy enough to provide meaningful at-bats isn’t helping.
The Dodgers are batting .215 through the first two games of the NLDS, with the Atlanta Braves scheduled to pitch left-handed ace Chris Sale in Game 3 on Tuesday. If the Dodgers lose, they would need to win back-to-back elimination games to advance beyond this series.
Roberts said the lineup changes he would consider include starting Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, both of whom hit well against left-handers. That could mean infielders Max Muncy (0 for 7 against Sale, with five strikeouts) and Tommy Edman (0 for 11 against Sale) might not start.
Center fielder Andy Pages, who batted so poorly last October he was benched for the final three games of the World Series, is hitless in seven at-bats in this series, with four strikeouts.
“I’m gonna continue to give Andy leash,” Roberts said. “I believe in him. I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we’re gonna need him to be an active part of our team.
Roberts said he did not envision benching catcher Will Smith, who is 0 for 8 in the series. The Dodgers’ backup catcher, Hunter Feduccia, is a career .205 hitter with no postseason experience.
But, even with the Dodgers’ star-studded lineup, the spotlight shines brightest on Ohtani.
Ohtani has not homered since Aug. 18. He hit .157 between then and the end of the regular season, striking out in 41% of his at-bats. In this series, he has two hits and two strikeouts in eight at-bats, and his inability to refrain from swinging at pitches outside the strike zone has become a glaring weakness.
“He’s not 100%,” Roberts said. “But, at the end of the day, he can still do a better job of staying in the strike zone.”
Ohtani hasn’t given the Braves a reason to challenge him within the strike zone.
“Everything orbits around Shohei, in the sense of his talent,” Roberts said. “And the Braves are going to enter with caution. And, so, knowing that, they’re going to continue to expand as long as we keep giving that to them. So until we show some discipline, they’re going to continue to kind of use that playbook.”

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Why Dodgers Top Prospect Josue De Paula Made NLDS Roster Over Dalton Rushing
item.dc:creator: J P Hoornstra; Unknown
item.description: Dalton Rushing's 2026 season has consisted of a few wildly different phases. item.content:encoded:
Dalton Rushing's 2026 season has consisted of a few wildly different phases. After Phase 1 — an eight-game stretch ending April 20 — the Los Angeles Dodgers' backup catcher had a .444 batting average, and an almost incomprehensible seven home runs in 28 plate appearances.
It was no surprise that Rushing couldn't maintain that torrid pace. What's surprising is what happened next — and how it resulted in his being left off the Dodgers' roster for the National League Division Series (and likely beyond).
Rookie Josue De Paula, not Rushing, is filling the role of manager Dave Roberts' left-handed pinch hitter off the bench against the Atlanta Braves. De Paula, 21, spent the season at Double-A Tulsa prior to his first big-league promotion in September. In 11 games with the Dodgers, he slashed .323/.500/.581.
"I think what we saw is a really good idea of the strike zone, quality of contact," Roberts said of De Paula. "I think that he's really unflappable, good heartbeat. I think that translates into the postseason."
Rushing was diagnosed with a partially torn UCL in his right (throwing) elbow in August. He tried to play through the injury, but catching was ultimately outside the realm of possibilities.
The Dodgers acquired two catchers, Hunter Feduccia and Ben Rortvedt, at the Aug. 3 trade deadline, and Feduccia is now the backup to Will Smith.
Rushing was able to avoid (or at least delay) surgery; that allowed him to hit even though he couldn't catch. However, the injury limited Rushing to only eight plate appearances after Aug. 1. His last hit was on July 30.
"Having eight at-bats in two months just put him behind the eight ball," Roberts said of Rushing. "The ability not to catch was something that also kind of worked against him. Great conversation with Dalton, great teammate, but I think those are the reasons for De Paula."
Overall, Rushing slashed .246/.328/.460. He hit only five home runs in 72 games after his early-season tear.
Even before the elbow injury, it was clear the league had adjusted to Rushing as a hitter (to say nothing of his sometimes questionable behavior between pitches).
The league hasn't adjusted to De Paula yet. How much that will matter in the postseason remains to be seen, but the Dodgers are impressed by what they've seen so far.
"The way he came up, obviously we think incredibly highly of him," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said, "and to see the calmness in his at-bats, the ability to look over baseball, the impact just felt like, as a bullet off the bench in big situations, just being able to trust the pulse and the ability."

J.P. Hoornstra is an On SI Contributor. A veteran of 20 years of sports coverage for daily newspapers in California, J.P. covered MLB, the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Los Angeles Angels (occasionally of Anaheim) from 2012-23 for the Southern California News Group. His first book, The 50 Greatest Dodgers Games of All-Time, published in 2015. In 2016, he won an Associated Press Sports Editors award for breaking news coverage. He once recorded a keyboard solo on the same album as two of the original Doors.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers heroes, zeros from Game 2 loss: Shohei Ohtani still looks off
Heroes, zeros and the inside pitch from the Dodgers’ 3–2 loss to the Atlanta Braves in Game 2 of the National League Division Series:
Zero
Shohei Ohtani’s first at-bat of this NLDS looked relatively normal, as he pulled a 105 mph line drive into right for a first-inning, Game 1 single.
Every subsequent trip to the plate, however, has been anything but.
Granted, Ohtani has not been the Dodgers’ biggest problem offensively. Will Smith (0–for–8), Andy Pages (0–for–7, one walk) and Tommy Edman (0–for–5, one walk) are all vying for that honor.
But if there was any hope that the team’s playoff-opening bye week would fix the two-way amid his ongoing right arm and left knee injuries, these two games have been a reminder of just how far he is from his typical self.
“I haven’t heard anything other than he feels fine,” manager Dave Roberts said.
But…
“I don’t know if he’s trying to do too much because he doesn’t feel perfect,” the skipper added, in what felt more like a tacit acknowledgement.
A healthy Ohtani, after all, wouldn’t go 0–for–2 against plucky feel-good story Ray Kerr, striking out on an inside fastball in the first inning before popping out in a key spot with two aboard in the third.
A healthy Ohtani wouldn’t need to slap the ball the other way Ichiro-style just to get a base hit, as he did on his lone single in the fifth.
The most telling thing for the 32-year-old superstar the last two days?
The Braves haven’t been afraid to challenge him, throwing him nine fastballs in the middle-third of the strike zone so far. And he hasn’t been able to punish them for it, turning only one into a hit (that first-inning, Game 1 single) while also chasing more outside of the zone after failing to end his at-bats.
“He’ll be in there Game 3,” Roberts confirmed. “We’ve just got to, again, take good at-bats and expect the best.”
Hero
At least the Dodgers’ other pre-NLDS injury question mark has seemingly turned a corner.
In his final 66 games of the regular season (going back to July 5), Freddie Freeman had hit only one home run. In September, he slumped to a .184 average with only one extra-base hit while battling a right knee injury that threatened to linger into the playoffs.
However, the bye week seemingly did wonders for him, following up a one-hit, one-walk performance in Game 1 of the series with a two-hit night Sunday that included a solo homer to right field.
“I feel good, so I think we can be done with those questions,” he quipped when asked about his swing and knee injury. “Just more consistently getting myself in a good spot, being able to put good swings on it.”
Unsung hero
There were times this year when Edwin Díaz’s fastball velocity dipped as low as 92 mph.
During his scoreless appearance in the sixth inning on Sunday, the resurgent right-hander dialed it up to a season-high 100.8 mph.
That was just one impressive aspect of Díaz’s latest standout performance, in which he extended his scoreless streak to six innings (including 15 straight batters retired over his last five outings) since returning from his second injured list stint of the year on Sept. 18.
“Edwin was great,” Roberts said. “I think if you look at tonight, try to find some silver linings, that was a silver lining and certainly a positive.”
Key stat
Zero: As in 0 hits with runners in scoring position for the Dodgers on Sunday, and 0 runs scored via any method other than a home run so far in this NLDS.
Ironically, the club’s lack of power had been the bigger concern coming into the playoffs.
While they could be (extremely) up-and-down in the regular season in situational at-bats, they still rank seventh in batting average with runners in scoring position and third in OPS.
That, however, hasn’t translated to October yet.
“Got to find a way to score some runs without hitting a home run,” Freeman said. “I think that’s our biggest thing right now.”
Quote of the night
“We’ve been in tougher spots than this one,” outfielder Teoscar Hernández said, when asked how crucial the team’s past October experience (especially in back-and-forth series like the 2024 NLDS and 2025 World Series) would be in the face of what is now a best-of-three showdown. “It’s a 1–1 series. We know they’re going to have the best pitcher that they have, starting pitcher, in [Game 3 with Chris] Sale. But we’re just gonna try to be ready and just go with the best plan and just try to execute it.”

item.content:encoded:
El colombiano Didier Fuentes lanzó tres entradas y dos tercios desde el bullpen de los Bravos de Atlanta, ponchó a Shohei Ohtani y ayudó a la victoria por 3-2 sobre los Dodgers de Los Ángeles en el Dodger Stadium. El resultado dejó igualada 1-1 la otra Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional.
Fuentes ingresó en el sexto episodio y permitió un imparable y una carrera limpia, sin otorgar bases por bolas. Realizó 47 lanzamientos, de los cuales 30 fueron strikes, y logró tres ponches durante su primera actuación de postemporada.
El relevista colombiano enfrentó a Ohtani con cuenta completa. Luego de una recta a 162,4 km/h, que fue declarada bola, recurrió a una bola curva 137,3 km/h, para conseguir el tercer strike.
También retiró por la vía del ponche a Will Smith y Freddie Freeman. Fuentes dominó a los primeros 11 bateadores que enfrentó, hasta que Max Muncy conectó un cuadrangular con dos outs en el noveno inning.
Esa es la racha más larga de un relevista de 21 años o menos en un juego de postemporada en la historia de la MLB. Ningún relevista de 21 años o menos ha tenido una racha tan larga en un juego de temporada regular desde Tom Gordon el 12 de abril de 1989, según lo publicado por Opta Stats en su perfil de X.
El único punto negativo de la jornada para el joven beisbolista cafetero fue el jonrón de Muncy impulsó la entrada de Iglesias, quien retiró al único bateador al que se enfrentó para conseguir la victoria. Pero eso no arruinó lo que fue una noche memorable para Fuentes, quien lanzó cuatro rectas a más de 99 mph en la novena entrada.
“Fue muy emotivo y emocionante. Así que le doy gracias a Dios por la ayuda que me ha permitido mantenerme sano y poder competir”, dijo el nacido en Tolú, Sucre, tras su primera gran noche en la liga más importante de béisbol en el mundo.
“¿Tiene 21 o 22 años? Está haciendo eso a esa edad. Es increíble, sobre todo lanzar a 100 millas por hora. Se enfrenta a situaciones de alto nivel y las supera. Fue realmente impresionante” dijo Kerr, el lanzador principal de los Bravos de Atlanta, sobre Fuentes.
Mientras que Matt Olson, primera base de los Bravos, se refirió a la potencia en el brazo que tiene el colombiano: “No podía creer que volviera a lanzar en la novena entrada, pero lo hizo y seguía lanzando a 100 millas por hora. Eso fue impresionante.”
“Después de su tercera entrada, miré a nuestro entrenador de lanzadores y le dije: ‘Veamos cómo se siente’”, dijo Weiss. “Si se siente bien, quiero que vuelva a lanzar. No quería cambiar algo que funcionaba bien. Estaba lanzando muy bien”, declaró el manager del equipo.
Los Bravos habían abierto el marcador con un sencillo productor de Mauricio Dubón en el primer episodio. Freeman igualó para los Dodgers con un jonrón solitario en el cuarto, pero Atlanta volvió a tomar la ventaja en el quinto mediante una jugada que permitió anotar a Michael Harris II.
Harris amplió el marcador en el séptimo con un doblete productor que llevó a Matt Olson al plato. Fuentes se anotó su primer hold, la estadística asignada a un relevista que preserva una ventaja en una situación comprometida. La serie se trasladará a Atlanta para el tercer juego, programado para el martes a las 5:00 p. m., hora de Colombia.
En las Series Divisionales con el formato actual 2-2-1, los equipos que consiguen dividir victorias como visitantes antes de regresar a casa para los Juegos 3 y 4 han ganado la serie 30 de 49 veces (61%).

item.content:encoded:
Now that the 2026 MLB regular season is done, Sony made one last ratings tweak for many of the players across the league on October 2. The October MLB The Show 26 ratings update saw Mookie Betts & Cade Smith rise to join the other Diamonds in the game.
The notable changes
Mookie Betts is back as a Diamond in MLB The Show 26. He and Cade Smith were the only two to move to Diamond status on October 2. Betts moved to 85 OVR after a strong final few weeks. Over his last 14 games, Betts slashed .316/.418/.632 with four home runs and 10 extra-base hits.
Smith, meanwhile, notched 41 saves and struck out 107 batters over 74 innings this season for the Guardians.
Fernando Tatis Jr. moved up three points between the last update and now. Tatis Jr., before the start of the playoffs, hit five home runs and nine extra-base hits in the last 15 games of the regular season for San Diego.
Elly De La Cruz, who had eight extra-base hits in the final two weeks, moved to 87 OVR, a +2 OVR increase. He moved there, along with NL Wild Card hero Michael Harris II.
As for who went down, Yandy Diaz and Jacob deGrom were both downgraded from Diamond status.

item.title: [clarosports.com] La gran interrogante de los Dodgers: ¿qué versión de Ohtani verán en la Serie Divisional ante Atlanta?
item.dc:creator: Julian Castillo
item.description: Ohtani busca recuperar su mejor versión ante Atlanta tras una campaña con lesiones que frenaron su impacto en los Dodgers. Los Angeles Dodgers ya conoce a su rival en la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional. Atlanta Braves superó la ronda de comodines y visitará Dodger Stadium este sábado 3 de octubre, en una serie al mejor de cinco juegos que abrirá a la 1:00 p.m. del Pacífico. Ahora, la atención de los fanáticos angelinos apunta a Shohei Ohtani y al nivel que podrá ofrecer después de un cierre
item.content:encoded:
Ohtani busca recuperar su mejor versión ante Atlanta tras una campaña con lesiones que frenaron su impacto en los Dodgers.
Los Angeles Dodgers ya conoce a su rival en la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional. Atlanta Braves superó la ronda de comodines y visitará Dodger Stadium este sábado 3 de octubre, en una serie al mejor de cinco juegos que abrirá a la 1:00 p.m. del Pacífico. Ahora, la atención de los fanáticos angelinos apunta a Shohei Ohtani y al nivel que podrá ofrecer después de un cierre de campaña marcado por molestias físicas.
El japonés completó una temporada productiva en términos generales, con promedio de .275, OPS de .889 y 30 jonrones, la cifra más alta del roster de los Dodgers. Sin embargo, su rendimiento quedó lejos de la continuidad que mostró en otros años, sobre todo durante el tramo final del calendario. Una lesión en el bíceps derecho y problemas en la rodilla izquierda afectaron su ritmo, limitaron su trabajo como lanzador y lo llevaron a la lista de lesionados.
Ohtani volvió para los últimos cinco juegos de la campaña regular, aunque sus números dejaron dudas. Bateó de 5-21, con un extrabase, una base por bolas y ocho ponches. Ese panorama pone el foco sobre su estado físico y su capacidad para convertirse de inmediato en un bate determinante frente a Atlanta.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Dodgers inician la defensa del bicampeonato: Braves o Phillies será su primer obstáculo
¿Cómo llega Shohei Ohtani a la Serie Divisional ante Braves?
La principal incógnita no tiene que ver con el talento de Ohtani, sino con su condición física después de un año exigente. El japonés arrastró molestias desde junio, cuando la rodilla izquierda comenzó a afectar su disponibilidad. Más tarde apareció el problema en el bíceps derecho, una lesión que tuvo impacto en su ofensiva y en su preparación para abrir juegos desde la lomita.
Los Dodgers decidieron actuar con cautela. Ohtani ingresó a la lista de lesionados de 15 días en septiembre y dejó de trabajar como pitcher. Su última apertura llegó el 3 de julio ante los San Diego Padres, partido en el que lanzó seis innings, permitió tres carreras y ponchó a nueve rivales antes de salir por tensión en el bíceps derecho.
La organización ya asumió que Ohtani no lanzará durante esta postemporada. Su aporte dependerá por completo de su trabajo como bateador designado, un rol que permite concentrar su recuperación en el ajuste ofensivo y reducir el desgaste físico. El propio jugador indicó durante septiembre que su prioridad sería el bateo, mientras los Dodgers proyectan que retome su faceta de dos vías en 2027.
Ese contexto eleva la importancia de cada turno. Los Dodgers necesitan a un Ohtani capaz de impactar el juego desde el primer lugar de la alineación, sobre todo ante una serie corta donde un mal inicio puede cambiar el rumbo de la eliminatoria.
¿Qué números tuvo Ohtani contra Atlanta en 2026?
Atlanta representa un reto incómodo para el japonés. Ohtani enfrentó a los Braves en seis juegos durante la temporada regular y conectó apenas cinco hits en 26 turnos, para un promedio de .192. Esa producción contrasta con sus números globales y refleja la dificultad que tuvo el lineup de Los Ángeles frente al pitcheo rival.
El problema tampoco quedó limitado a Ohtani. Los Braves dominaron la serie particular ante los Dodgers con cinco victorias en seis enfrentamientos y una diferencia de carreras de 26-15. Atlanta llega con la confianza de haber encontrado una fórmula efectiva contra el campeón defensor, aunque los playoffs representan un escenario distinto y Dodger Stadium recibirá los dos primeros juegos.
El bajo promedio del japonés ante Atlanta no define lo que puede ocurrir en octubre, pero sí señala un punto de atención. Ohtani deberá mejorar la calidad de sus turnos, siendo más selectivo en los lanzamiento que ataca para poder hacer daño. En una ofensiva con figuras como Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts y Will Smith, su presencia en circulación puede abrir oportunidades para el resto del orden.
Los Dodgers tampoco requieren que cargue solo con el ataque. Su tarea inmediata pasa por recuperar consistencia, seleccionar mejor los pitcheos y ofrecer una amenaza constante en cada aparición al plato.
¿Cuándo juegan Dodgers vs. Atlanta Braves en la Serie Divisional?
Los Angeles Dodgers abrirá la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional ante los Atlanta Braves este sábado 3 de octubre en Dodger Stadium. El Juego 1 comenzará a las 4:00 p.m., hora del Este, con los angelinos como locales tras asegurar la ventaja de localía.
- Juego 2: domingo 4 de octubre, Braves vs. Dodgers, 8:00 p.m. hora del Este, Dodger Stadium
- Juego 3: martes 6 de octubre, Dodgers vs. Braves, 6:00 p.m. hora del Este, Truist Park
- Juego 4: miércoles 7 de octubre, Dodgers vs. Braves, 6:00 p.m. hora del Este, Truist Park, si es necesario
- Juego 5: viernes 9 de octubre, Braves vs. Dodgers, 8:00 p.m. hora del Este, Dodger Stadium, si es necesario
¿El descanso puede ayudar a Ohtani con Dodgers?
La mejor noticia para Los Ángeles llegó con el calendario. El equipo aseguró el primer sembrado de la Liga Nacional y obtuvo cinco días de descanso antes del inicio de la Serie Divisional. Ese margen le permitió a Ohtani descansar después de volver de la lista de lesionados y trabajar en su swing sin la presión diaria de la temporada regular.
Dave Roberts espera una versión más saludable de su estrella para el sábado. La pausa no elimina por completo las dudas sobre el bíceps y la rodilla, aunque sí ofrece una ventana útil para que el japonés llegue con mayor frescura. El club también tiene margen para administrar su carga física durante una serie que contempla días de descanso entre los primeros compromisos.
La serie comienza el sábado en Los Ángeles con un duelo que marcará el tono de la eliminatoria. Ohtani no tendrá responsabilidad desde el montículo, pero su presencia en el primer turno de la alineación será una de las claves ofensivas del equipo. El descanso abre una oportunidad para que el japonés deje atrás un cierre irregular y responda en el momento que más importa para los Dodgers.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Projecting the Dodgers' NLDS roster with Josue De Paula, bench shuffle
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers get to kick back and watch as eight teams duke it out to move on to their respective League Division Series this week. The Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies will go head-to-head in the NL Wild Card Series before one of them moves on to try and topple LA. One would think that this Dodgers team would have everything buttoned up well ahead of the NLDS, but there are still a couple of key questions to be answered. Projecting the Dodgers' NLDS roster with Josue De Paula
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers get to kick back and watch as eight teams duke it out to move on to their respective League Division Series this week. The Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies will go head-to-head in the NL Wild Card Series before one of them moves on to try and topple LA.
One would think that this Dodgers team would have everything buttoned up well ahead of the NLDS, but there are still a couple of key questions to be answered.
Projecting the Dodgers' NLDS roster with Josue De Paula called upon
Catchers (2): Will Smith, Hunter Feduccia
For some reason, the Dodgers decided to carry three catchers on their Wild Card and NLDS rosters last year — Smith, Dalton Rushing, and Ben Rortvedt — but adjusted ahead of the NLCS by shedding Rushing, who received just one at-bat in the NLDS but otherwise rode the bench.
Rortvedt didn't get a start or even substitution after Game 2 of the NLDS with Smith slowly coming back from injury at the beginning of the postseason. Feduccia figures to play a similar break-glass-in-case-of-emergency role. As a lefty, he could get a start and then an early pull depending on matchups but, barring disaster, it's mostly going to be Smith's show.
Designated hitters (2): Shohei Ohtani, Josue De Paula
The Dodgers clearly want to find a way to bring De Paula with them in October, even if only as a lingering threat on their bench. They're reportedly not entertaining putting him in the outfield at all, and it's not hard to see why. Even if they're confident they'll be able to fix his defense in time, they can't afford any leakage in the postseason.
Ohtani is still shaking off the cobwebs from his 15-day IL stint. He picked up a few hits with promising exit velocity in his return against the San Diego Padres and later against the San Francisco Giants, but there are still question marks around what version of him we might see this postseason.
Infielders (6): Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, Tommy Edman, Max Muncy, Miguel Rojas, Kiké Hernández
A notable exclusion here is Hyeseong Kim. Although he's in the running to get a spot on the bench and exclusively come into games to pinch-run or for reassurances on defense, there's still a chance he doesn't make the roster if the Dodgers are set on carrying 13 pitchers. Edman and Hernández, though lacking the same speed as Kim, can still offer the same defensive versatility.
Outfielders (3): Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Teoscar Hernández
Pages might've found himself in the same boat as Ohtani, but he announced his return to the Dodgers after a month-long IL stint in a big way, hitting .333 with a 1.180 OPS, two homers, and five RBI against the Padres and Giants. No doubt Dave Roberts and Andrew Friedman breathed a massive sigh of relief.
Alex Call will be the odd man out. He was on all four of LA's playoff rosters last year and received sporadic appearances throughout the month, but that was when Michael Conforto was still on the payroll. Tucker and Hernández have certainly had their ups-and-downs this season, but the Dodgers would never seriously consider leaving them out.
Starters (4): Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal, Tyler Glasnow
There's not much to say about what's probably the best rotation going into the postseason. Snell and Glasnow have both battled injury this season but came back when the Dodgers needed them most. It might be too much to ask that any of Yamamoto, Snell, or Glasnow replicate their dominance from last year, but they'll certainly try.
Relievers: (9): Tanner Scott, Roki Sasaki, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Justin Wrobleski, Edwin Díaz, Kris Bubic, Edgardo Henriquez
Just like 2025, this is where things get dicey. The Dodgers' bullpen isn't quite as banged up or as unreliable as they were last year, but they're not the air-tight, bulletproof coterie that their combined salaries suggest they should be. Henriquez will be coming straight off of the IL to rejoin the team in the NLDS, and Díaz, Sasaki, and Scott are all woefully unpredictable.
There is some thought that the Dodgers might carry eight relievers instead of nine, to free up a spot on the position player side for a guy like Kim. In this scenario, we'll stick with them taking nine. If not, Bubic is the most obvious cut. Last one in, first one out.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Locked in as No. 2 seed, Dodgers turn to Tarik Skubal vs. Giants
item.description: Having seen their chances of gaining the top seed in the National League playoffs die in a two-game span, the Los Angeles Dodgers get an opportunity to coast into the postseason when they open a three-game road set against the San Francisco Giants on Friday. item.content:encoded:
Having seen their chances of gaining the top seed in the National League playoffs die in a two-game span, the Los Angeles Dodgers get an opportunity to coast into the postseason when they open a three-game road set against the San Francisco Giants on Friday.
Left-hander Tarik Skubal (11-7, 2.85 ERA) is scheduled to get his final tune-up for the postseason in the series opener for the Dodgers. He will be opposed by Giants right-hander Yunior Marte (0-1, 4.66).
While they can’t overtake the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record, the Dodgers (97-62) have clinched the NL West title and the second-best record in the league. The latter will earn them a first-round bye in the playoffs, meaning after Sunday’s regular-season finale in San Francisco, they won’t play again until next Saturday.
Skubal will be making his 10th start since he was acquired from the Detroit Tigers at the trade deadline. Los Angeles has won seven of his nine outings, including the last six.
Skubal wasn’t particularly effective in a five-inning start against the Giants last Saturday in which he allowed four runs, two on a home run by Victor Bericoto. The Dodgers supported him with seven runs in those five innings, allowing him to walk away with a win.
He has faced the Giants just three times in his career, going 2-1 with a 4.30 ERA.
Skubal should have additional firepower supporting him in the rematch as the Dodgers have brought Shohei Ohtani and Andy Pages back from injuries over the last three days.
Each got extensive playing time in the just-completed home series against the Padres, with Pages playing in all three games and Ohtani the last two, each going 3-for-9.
Both are expected to play significantly against the Giants, with the team getting five days off to start next week.
“I think we all know why it’s important,” Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman said about the importance of the first-round bye. “There’s a lot of us kind of limping toward the end here. It’s good to get those guys (Ohtani and Pages) back on the field, get some ABs in them and then rest up.”
Skubal will be matched up once again with Marte, who allowed six runs in 4 2/3 innings in the meeting in Los Angeles last week. A rookie facing the Dodgers for the first time, he served up a home run to Will Smith in taking the loss in his fourth major league appearance.
The Dodgers could see a familiar face late in the game with the Giants on Thursday having claimed their former closer, Camilo Doval, on waivers from the Pirates.
After 4 1/2 seasons in San Francisco in which he recorded 107 saves and was an All-Star in 2023, the Giants sent Doval to the New York Yankees last July for four prospects. One year and one day later, the Yankees flipped the right-hander to Pittsburgh, which in turn saw him pitch just 20 times before cutting him loose, allowing the Giants to snatch him back.
Interestingly, should Doval or another newcomer — catcher Zach Morgan — get into a game during the Dodgers series, the Giants (65-94) would tie the major-league record for number of players used in a season with 71. Should they both play, they would break the record.
Giants manager Tony Vitello joked to reporters Wednesday about the possibility of setting the record.
“I guess, you know, being the first year in the organization, you’d like to get to meet everybody,” he said. “So this is one way to do it.”
–Field Level Media

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dodgers' Josue De Paula update all but confirms his postseason roster spot
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers completed their sweep over the San Francisco Giants on Sunday in extra innings. It was their sixth time reaching the century-mark during the last decade, which is better than any American League team and second only to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League. The Dodgers now have four days to game plan before they take on either the Philadelphia Phillies or the Atlanta Braves in the NLDS at Dodger Stadium. There could be some surprises in store, especially on the bul
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers completed their sweep over the San Francisco Giants on Sunday in extra innings. It was their sixth time reaching the century-mark during the last decade, which is better than any American League team and second only to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League.
The Dodgers now have four days to game plan before they take on either the Philadelphia Phillies or the Atlanta Braves in the NLDS at Dodger Stadium.
There could be some surprises in store, especially on the bullpen front. Blake Treinen's season just ended with a shoulder issue, Edwin Díaz has enjoyed a resurgence since coming off the IL, Edgardo Henriquez is trending toward availability, and they still need to figure out the Roki Sasaki of it all.
But fans saw all of that coming. The more interesting roster development in the last week has been the battle of the No. 1 prospects: Josue De Paula vs. Dalton Rushing.
De Paula was optioned back to Triple-A after Shohei Ohtani came off the IL, and Rushing was officially reactivated from the IL ahead of the Giants series. De Paula, however, looks like he still has the upper hand here, and will be in LA during the bye week as the Dodgers consider all of their options.
Josue De Paula is on track to win Dodgers' postseason roster battle
The Dodgers are currently carrying three catchers: Rushing, Will Smith, and Hunter Feduccia. Whoever LA chooses to be the backup catcher, that player will be playing second fiddle to Smith (even more than they already do).
Last year, Ben Rortvedt started two games in the NL Wild Card Series while Smith came back from an injury, but he didn't make an appearance past Game 2 of the NLDS. Feduccia, though more dispensable than Rushing in most contexts, makes more sense in that role.
LA wants a big lefty bat they can keep on the bench, and De Paula established himself as the better bet almost immediately. At the same time, Rushing had the disadvantage of being on the IL, unable to state his own case.
The question is how the Dodgers will petition the Commissioner's Office to carry De Paula on the roster. He'll have to replace an injured player who's already served the minimum amount of time on the IL. In bringing Rushing back, the Dodgers needlessly complicated things.
But no doubt Andrew Friedman will figure it out. De Paula might only get a precious few at-bats throughout the month, but they clearly already trust him.

item.dc:creator: Blake Williams
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have a chance to repeat with Roberto Clemente Award winners this season. It is presented annually in recognition of the Major League player who best represents the game of baseball through extraordinary character, community involvement, philanth
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have a chance to repeat with Roberto Clemente Award winners this season.
Will Smith is the Dodgers’ nominee to win the prestigious honor this year, while Mookie Betts was named the 2025 Roberto Clemente Award winner.
The Roberto Clemente Award is considered baseball’s most prestigious individual honor. It is presented annually in recognition of the Major League player who best represents the game of baseball through extraordinary character, community involvement, philanthropy and positive contributions, both on and off the field.
Each team nominates one player to be considered for the league-wide award in tribute to Clemente’s achievements and character.
The Dodgers have had for players to win the award in history, with Betts being the most recent. Before that, it was Justin Turner who took the honor in 2022.
Major League Baseball continued its recognition of past Clemente Award winners and reached out to some of them on Instagram, asking what it means to be a winner.
Both Betts and Turner were among those who replied as part of the social media campaign.
“It means a lot… it means you are helping communities and it’s always cool to be recognized for the work you put in off the field,” Betts wrote in his reply to MLB. “Baseball is baseball, but being a good human is central to life.”
“For me it’s the greatest honor in the game because Roberto set the bar for what it means to take our platform, this beautiful gift of playing a game for a living, and use it to give back to those in need,” Turner wrote in his reply. “He took his star power and used it to lift up those in need and enduring difficult times! Roberto was a humanitarian who happened to be great at baseball!!!!”
Former Dodgers Curtis Granderson and Jimmy Rollins, who won the award with different teams, also shared their perspectives in the post. In addition, Nelson Cruz, who currently works in the Dodgers’ player development system, shared his insight.
Along with Betts and Turner, the other Dodgers to win the award were Clayton Kershaw (2012) and Steve Garvey (1981).
Roberto Clemente Award selection process
A panel of sportswriters and baseball dignitaries selects the winner of the Roberto Clemente Award. In addition, there is a fan vote element that counts as one vote among those cast by the blue-ribbon panel.
Fan voting ended on Sunday, the final day of the 2026 regular season.
The league-wide winner of the Roberto Clemente Award will be honored at the 2026 World Series following selection by the aforementioned panel.
It includes representatives from the commissioner’s office, Capital One, MLB-affiliated networks (MLB Network, FOX Sports, ESPN and TBS), MLB.com, National Baseball Hall of Fame, as well as Roberto’s children, Enrique, Luis and Roberto Clemente, Jr.
If you love our reporting, choose DodgerBlue.com as a preferred source on Google.

item.title: [Yardbarker] Dodgers Make Sudden Freddie Freeman Announcement
item.dc:creator: Simeon Kotto
item.description: Freddie Freeman is back where the Los Angeles Dodgers like him: in the middle of a loaded order, on the last afternoon of the regular season. After sitting Saturday against the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers first baseman is in Sunday’s Game 162 lineup at Oracle Park and batting third. The card posted by Underdog MLB puts Shohei Ohtani at designated hitter, Mookie Betts at shortstop, Freeman at first, Kyle Tucker in right, Teoscar Hernández in left, Max Muncy at third, Andy Pages in center, H
item.content:encoded:
Freddie Freeman is back where the Los Angeles Dodgers like him: in the middle of a loaded order, on the last afternoon of the regular season.
After sitting Saturday against the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers first baseman is in Sunday’s Game 162 lineup at Oracle Park and batting third.
The card posted by Underdog MLB puts Shohei Ohtani at designated hitter, Mookie Betts at shortstop, Freeman at first, Kyle Tucker in right, Teoscar Hernández in left, Max Muncy at third, Andy Pages in center, Hunter Feduccia behind the plate and Tommy Edman at second. Jack Dreyer is listed as the starter in what figures to be a bullpen game.
The off day was not a surprise. Freeman had started each of the previous 10 games and was dragging a .522 OPS over 45 plate appearances in that stretch.
Enrique Hernández filled in at first on Saturday while the club gave its 37-year-old cornerstone a breather.
That is how Dave Roberts has handled September: keep Freeman available, not exhausted, with the postseason a few days away.
Sunday’s assignment is the one Freeman has occupied for most of his career.
He has started more than 1,300 games in the three-hole across Atlanta and Los Angeles, and even after spring talk about a cleanup role behind Tucker, the Dodgers keep sliding him back between Betts and the middle of the order when they want their most reliable left-handed bat seeing traffic.
He entered the weekend hitting .290 with 167 hits, 16 homers and 70 RBIs. The power has been quieter lately — he has gone without an extra-base hit for more than two weeks — but the bat-to-ball skill is still the reason Los Angeles trusts him with runners on.
The context around the lineup is October-minded. Los Angeles is 99-62 and chasing a 100-win season in the finale. Will Smith is the only everyday starter sitting.
Blake Treinen is headed to the injured list with a shoulder issue, so the bullpen will be asked to work. First pitch is 12:05 p.m. PT / 3:05 p.m. ET on SportsNet LA.
For Freeman, the message is simple. One rest day. Then back in the three-hole, glove at first, with Ohtani and Betts in front of him and Tucker behind him.
If the Dodgers are going to finish 100-62 and carry momentum into the NLDS, they want their veteran first baseman in the middle of it — not on the bench, and not buried in the order.
Sunday is a tune-up with meaning: one more look at the group that has to win in October.

5. Kyle Tucker, RF
6. Miguel Rojas, 3B
7. Andy Pages, CF
8. Kike Hernandez, 1B
9. Tommy Edman, 2B
The Dodgers are facing lefty Matt Wilkinson, which lets Rojas and Kike Hernandez enter the mix in a favorable matchup with a righty-heavy lineup.
The biggest note of the game is that once again, Mookie Betts is batting leadoff, while Shohei Ohtani is hitting second.
Manager Dave Roberts has made it clear that Ohtani wasn’t guaranteed to hit leadoff against lefties, and with Betts continuing to deliver quality plate appearances, the Dodgers skipper is willing to start the order with Betts.
At-bats from Andy Pages, Kike Hernandez, Miguel Rojas, and Tommy Edman are all worth monitoring. Pages is still somewhat fresh off the injured list, while Tommy Edman has been in a slump.
Rojas and Hernandez feature so inconsistently that they are always worth following whenever they play.
Who is pitching for the Dodgers?
Blake Snell starts against the Giants after being pulled early in his last outing. Snell, who has a history of groin injuries, had some groin soreness surface against the Cincinnati Reds last week.
Initial concern about his postseason viability grew, and as a key member of the rotation, the Dodgers could ill-afford to lose him.
The injury doesn’t seem major, and Snell has a chance to get some pitching work before October kicks into high gear.
In terms of actual pitching production, Snell sits at the top, with elite stuff and sharp command.
If he is fully sharp, Snell can carry a team in the postseason, and while the Dodgers don’t need that this week, next week will be a different story.

item.dc:creator: Gabe Smallson; Unknown

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 2-0, on Friday night and improved to 98-62 on the year.
Two-time Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal unleashed another masterpiece with seven scoreless innings, 10 strikeouts, no walks and just three hits allowed. Offensively, Will Smith had a three-hit evening while two second inning solo home runs were collected by Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages (his first home run since being activated off the injured list).
Ahead of Friday's game, the Dodgers demoted an infielder to make room on the roster to activate catcher Dalton Rushing. Manager Dave Roberts spoke on the kind of role fans can expect from Rushing down the stretch.
“At the most it would be three pinch-hit at-bats, so just conduct at-bats and see what you got,” Roberts said. “Just the circumstances of his situation, it’s just tough to just be hurt, come back, then be hurt again, and then take three pinch-hit at-bats to potentially then say, ‘Hey, you’re on the roster.’"
Additionally, Roberts had a message for rookie Josue De Paula after he was optioned to Triple-A following a productive first 11 games at the major league level. The reasoning, he revealed, was that De Paula could act as a spark plug while superstar Shohei Ohtani was on the injured list — and during his time on the shelf, it's exactly what the 21-year-old provided.
“This was the original thought, that once Shohei gets back, we’re going to send him out,” Roberts said. “We had a runway to give him, which we gave him and he performed more than admirably. This also, as far as the timing, just gives us an opportunity to potentially have him back for the postseason. He’s a part of the conversation, and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him last night.”
Finally, there is an update on southpaw Blake Snell after he lasted just one inning due to groin discomfort during his most recent start. Luckily for Dodgers fans, the team announced that Snell will make his next scheduled start on Saturday during the penultimate regular season game.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Commentary: Dodgers' three-peat hopes rest on their four aces — and bottom-of-order production
item.dc:creator: Bill Shaikin
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - - The Dodgers’ path to a third straight World Series title will depend on four frontline starters, but manager Dave Roberts hopes his offense won’t leave them carrying the load. - In a 2-0 win over San Francisco, Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages offered a timely reminder that the Dodgers will need consistent production from the bottom half of the lineup in the playoffs. - Hernández is a proven October hitter, while Pages is finding his swing after c
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- The Dodgers’ path to a third straight World Series title will depend on four frontline starters, but manager Dave Roberts hopes his offense won’t leave them carrying the load.
- In a 2-0 win over San Francisco, Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages offered a timely reminder that the Dodgers will need consistent production from the bottom half of the lineup in the playoffs.
- Hernández is a proven October hitter, while Pages is finding his swing after coming back from a broken hand.
SAN FRANCISCO — This is the 60th anniversary of the 1966 World Series, in which the losing team did not score for the final 33 innings of the series.
That losing team was the Dodgers. Over the final three games of the series, Jim Palmer, Wally Bunker and Dave McNally of the Baltimore Orioles each pitched a complete-game shutout.
That art of pitching is not in style today. Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched two complete games last October, but he cannot pitch every game, even if he left that impression upon the Toronto Blue Jays.
The Dodgers’ clearest and cleanest route to a three-peat nonetheless rests upon the four shoulders of Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. If the four aces can do to October opponents what the 1966 Orioles did to the Dodgers, or some reasonable 21st century facsimile, we’ll see you at the parade.
Does Dodgers manager Dave Roberts believe his starting pitchers will have to carry the load in October?
“I hope not,” Roberts said.
Tarik Skubal gives up just three hits and strikes out 10 in his final start before the postseason to help carry the Dodgers to a 2-0 win over the Giants.
Friday’s 2-0 victory over the San Francisco Giants offered two encouraging swings. Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages each hit home runs, a reminder that a properly tuned Dodgers offense runs on more than Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and Will Smith.
Skubal scattered three hits and struck out 10 in seven scoreless innings, which would have gone for naught without the Hernández and Pages home runs. Given that the Dodgers were playing the Giants and the remains of their depleted roster, it was something of a warning sign: this could happen against a postseason team.
No team can plan to score a lot of runs against the Dodgers’ starters. The opposing game plan would be to neutralize them and keep the game close enough to where one or two big swings can make the difference. The Giants, who have the National League’s second-worst record, almost pulled it off.
“When you get to the postseason, they’re going to try to eliminate Shohei and try to make other guys beat you,” Roberts said. “So it always sort of comes to the middle to the bottom of the order, where you’ve either got to get guys on base or get hits, get big hits.”
In October, Hernández is who you want at bat. He has homered in six of the seven postseason series he has played for the Dodgers, including each of the last five. In 33 postseason games for the Dodgers, he has driven in 25 runs.
For most players, offensive production drops in October, when batters face the best pitchers from the best teams. For Hernández, his career OPS is .796 in the regular season and .792 in the postseason.
And, for all his summer struggles, he is batting .354 this month, with an OPS just shy of 1.000. He’ll be, as the league-issued hoodies used to say, October ready.
For Pages, however, last October was cruel.
This October was not looking particularly promising, either. Pages missed 27 games because of a broken hand, leaving him the final six games of the regular season to get his swing back into rhythm.
“You think that you take five weeks off,” Roberts said, “that your timing is going to be off a little bit.”
So far, so good: five hits in 12 at-bats, including the home run Friday.
Pages ended the regular season last year with four hits in his final 28 at-bats. That, Roberts said, tells him this October will be different for Pages.
“I think the one thing is the confidence, how he went into last October really scuffling, and it sort of bled into October,” Roberts said, “where I think right now he feels really confident, swinging the bat well, and the hope is that this one bleeds into October as well.
“So, I think it’s definitely a different result going into October, and then also his headspace. There’s a lot more confidence this year.”
In 2025, when the Dodgers won the World Series, they ranked second among the 30 major league clubs in runs scored, and in home runs. In 2024, when they won the World Series, they ranked third in runs scored, and in home runs.
The Dodgers rank fourth in runs scored this year, and seventh in home runs. The offense is down some, if not much. In all the national postseason hype, the Dodgers projections will boil down to one sentence: Can anyone stop those starters?
“I think at first glance that’s what you see in our ballclub,” Roberts said. “But we have a lot of talented, really good hitters and I hope they work hand in hand and not just our pitching and defense carry us.”
For the Dodgers, the postseason opens one week from Saturday. If the Dodgers roll out the 1966 playbook, their October stay will be short.
